gene.name: ATP binding cassette subfamily A member 1
gene.function: Catalyzes the translocation of specific phospholipids from the cytoplasmic to the extracellular/lumenal leaflet of membrane coupled to the hydrolysis of ATP. Thereby, participates in phospholipid transfer to apolipoproteins to form nascent high density lipoproteins/HDLs. Transports preferentially phosphatidylcholine over phosphatidylserine. May play a similar role in the efflux of intracellular cholesterol to apolipoproteins and the formation of nascent high density lipoproteins/HDLs. Translocates phospholipids from the outer face of the plasma membrane and forces it through its gateway and annulus into an elongated hydrophobic tunnel in its extracellular domain.

gene.name: angiotensin converting enzyme 2
gene.function: Essential counter-regulatory carboxypeptidase of the renin- angiotensin hormone system that is a critical regulator of blood volume, systemic vascular resistance, and thus cardiovascular homeostasis. Converts angiotensin I to angiotensin 1- 9, a nine-amino acid peptide with anti-hypertrophic effects in cardiomyocytes, and angiotensin II to angiotensin 1-7, which then acts as a beneficial vasodilator and anti-proliferation agent, counterbalancing the actions of the vasoconstrictor angiotensin II. Also removes the C-terminal residue from three other vasoactive peptides, neurotensin, kinetensin, and des-Arg bradykinin, but is not active on bradykinin. Also cleaves other biological peptides, such as apelins (apelin-13, [Pyr1]apelin-13, apelin-17, apelin-36), casomorphins (beta-casomorphin- 7, neocasomorphin) and dynorphin A with high efficiency. In addition, ACE2 C-terminus is homologous to collectrin and is responsible for the trafficking of the neutral amino acid transporter SL6A19 to the plasma membrane of gut epithelial cells via direct interaction, regulating its expression on the cell surface and its catalytic activity.

gene.name: CD36 molecule (CD36 blood group)
gene.function: Multifunctional glycoprotein that acts as a receptor for a broad range of ligands. Ligands can be of proteinaceous nature like thrombospondin, fibronectin, collagen or amyloid-beta as well as of lipidic nature such as oxidized low-density lipoprotein (oxLDL), anionic phospholipids, long- and very long-chain fatty acids and bacterial diacylated lipopeptides. They are generally multivalent and can therefore engage multiple receptors simultaneously, the resulting formation of CD36 clusters initiates signal transduction and internalization of receptor-ligand complexes. The dependency on coreceptor signaling is strongly ligand specific. Cellular responses to these ligands are involved in angiogenesis, inflammatory response, fatty acid metabolism, taste and dietary fat processing in the intestine (Probable). Binds long- and very long-chain fatty acids and facilitates their transport into cells, thus participating in muscle lipid utilization, adipose energy storage, and gut fat absorption (By similarity). Mechanistically, palmitoylated CD36 captures fatty acids on the cell surface, the binding of fatty acids activates downstream kinase LYN, which phosphorylates the palmitoyltransferase ZDHHC5 and inactivates it, resulting in the subsequent depalmitoylation of CD36, a step needed to initiate the endocytic process and delivery of fatty acids into the cell. In the small intestine, plays a role in proximal absorption of dietary fatty acid and cholesterol for optimal chylomicron formation, possibly through the activation of MAPK1/3 (ERK1/2) signaling pathway (By similarity). Involved in oral fat perception and preferences. Detection into the tongue of long-chain fatty acids leads to a rapid and sustained rise in flux and protein content of pancreatobiliary secretions (By similarity). In taste receptor cells, mediates the induction of an increase in intracellular calcium levels by long-chain fatty acids, leading to the activation of the gustatory neurons in the nucleus of the solitary tract (By similarity). Important factor in both ventromedial hypothalamus neuronal sensing of long-chain fatty acid and the regulation of energy and glucose homeostasis (By similarity). Receptor for thrombospondins, THBS1 and THBS2, mediating their antiangiogenic effects (By similarity). Involved in inducing apoptosis in podocytes in response to elevated free fatty acids, acting together with THBS1 (By similarity). As a coreceptor for TLR4:TLR6 heterodimer, promotes inflammation in monocytes/macrophages. Upon ligand binding, such as oxLDL or amyloid-beta 42, interacts with the heterodimer TLR4:TLR6, the complex is internalized and triggers inflammatory response, leading to NF-kappa-B-dependent production of CXCL1, CXCL2 and CCL9 cytokines, via MYD88 signaling pathway, and CCL5 cytokine, via TICAM1 signaling pathway, as well as IL1B secretion, through the priming and activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome (By similarity). Selective and nonredundant sensor of microbial diacylated lipopeptide that signal via TLR2:TLR6 heterodimer, this cluster triggers signaling from the cell surface, leading to the NF-kappa-B-dependent production of TNF, via MYD88 signaling pathway and subsequently is targeted to the Golgi in a lipid-raft dependent pathway (By similarity).

gene.name: complement factor H related 5
gene.function: Involved in complement regulation. The dimerized forms have avidity for tissue-bound complement fragments and efficiently compete with the physiological complement inhibitor CFH. .

gene.name: collagen type I alpha 1 chain
gene.function: Type I collagen is a member of group I collagen (fibrillar forming collagen).

gene.name: collagen type IV alpha 3 chain
gene.function: Type IV collagen is the major structural component of glomerular basement membranes (GBM), forming a 'chicken-wire' meshwork together with laminins, proteoglycans and entactin/nidogen.

gene.name: cathepsin S
gene.function: Thiol protease. Key protease responsible for the removal of the invariant chain from MHC class II molecules and MHC class II antigen presentation. The bond- specificity of this proteinase is in part similar to the specificities of cathepsin L. Elicits itch by mediating cleavage and activation of MRGPRX1 (By similarity). .

gene.name: discoidin domain receptor tyrosine kinase 1
gene.function: Tyrosine kinase that functions as a cell surface receptor for fibrillar collagen and regulates cell attachment to the extracellular matrix, remodeling of the extracellular matrix, cell migration, differentiation, survival and cell proliferation. Collagen binding triggers a signaling pathway that involves SRC and leads to the activation of MAP kinases. Regulates remodeling of the extracellular matrix by up-regulation of the matrix metalloproteinases MMP2, MMP7 and MMP9, and thereby facilitates cell migration and wound healing. Required for normal blastocyst implantation during pregnancy, for normal mammary gland differentiation and normal lactation. Required for normal ear morphology and normal hearing (By similarity). Promotes smooth muscle cell migration, and thereby contributes to arterial wound healing. Also plays a role in tumor cell invasion. Phosphorylates PTPN11.

gene.name: FYN proto-oncogene, Src family tyrosine kinase
gene.function: Non-receptor tyrosine-protein kinase that plays a role in many biological processes including regulation of cell growth and survival, cell adhesion, integrin-mediated signaling, cytoskeletal remodeling, cell motility, immune response and axon guidance. Inactive FYN is phosphorylated on its C-terminal tail within the catalytic domain. Following activation by PKA, the protein subsequently associates with PTK2/FAK1, allowing PTK2/FAK1 phosphorylation, activation and targeting to focal adhesions. Involved in the regulation of cell adhesion and motility through phosphorylation of CTNNB1 (beta-catenin) and CTNND1 (delta-catenin). Regulates cytoskeletal remodeling by phosphorylating several proteins including the actin regulator WAS and the microtubule-associated proteins MAP2 and MAPT. Promotes cell survival by phosphorylating AGAP2/PIKE- A and preventing its apoptotic cleavage. Participates in signal transduction pathways that regulate the integrity of the glomerular slit diaphragm (an essential part of the glomerular filter of the kidney) by phosphorylating several slit diaphragm components including NPHS1, KIRREL1 and TRPC6. Plays a role in neural processes by phosphorylating DPYSL2, a multifunctional adapter protein within the central nervous system, ARHGAP32, a regulator for Rho family GTPases implicated in various neural functions, and SNCA, a small pre-synaptic protein. Involved in reelin signaling by mediating phosphorylation of DAB1 following reelin (RELN)- binding to its receptor (By similarity). Participates in the downstream signaling pathways that lead to T-cell differentiation and proliferation following T-cell receptor (TCR) stimulation. Phosphorylates PTK2B/PYK2 in response to T-cell receptor activation. Also participates in negative feedback regulation of TCR signaling through phosphorylation of PAG1 and PDCD1. Phosphorylation of PAG1 promotes interaction between PAG1 and CSK and recruitment of CSK to lipid rafts. Phosphorylation of PDCD1 leads to the recruitment of PTPN11/SHP-2 that mediates dephosphorylation of key TCR proximal signaling molecules. CSK maintains LCK and FYN in an inactive form (By similarity). Promotes CD28-induced phosphorylation of VAV1. In mast cells, phosphorylates CLNK after activation of immunoglobulin epsilon receptor signaling (By similarity). Can also promote CD244-mediated NK cell activation.

gene.name: inverted formin 2
gene.function: Severs actin filaments and accelerates their polymerization and depolymerization. .

gene.name: laminin subunit alpha 5
gene.function: Binding to cells via a high affinity receptor, laminin is thought to mediate the attachment, migration and organization of cells into tissues during embryonic development by interacting with other extracellular matrix components. Plays a role in the regulation of skeletogenesis, through a mechanism that involves integrin-mediated signaling and PTK2B/PYK2. .

gene.name: matrix metallopeptidase 1
gene.function: Cleaves collagens of types I, II, and III at one site in the helical domain. Also cleaves collagens of types VII and X. In case of HIV infection, interacts and cleaves the secreted viral Tat protein, leading to a decrease in neuronal Tat's mediated neurotoxicity.

gene.name: matrix metallopeptidase 9
gene.function: Matrix metalloproteinase that plays an essential role in local proteolysis of the extracellular matrix and in leukocyte migration. Could play a role in bone osteoclastic resorption (By similarity). Cleaves KiSS1 at a Gly-|-Leu bond. Cleaves NINJ1 to generate the Secreted ninjurin-1 form. Cleaves type IV and type V collagen into large C-terminal three quarter fragments and shorter N- terminal one quarter fragments. Degrades fibronectin but not laminin or Pz-peptide.

gene.name: NPHS1 adhesion molecule, nephrin
gene.function: Seems to play a role in the development or function of the kidney glomerular filtration barrier. Regulates glomerular vascular permeability. May anchor the podocyte slit diaphragm to the actin cytoskeleton. Plays a role in skeletal muscle formation through regulation of myoblast fusion (By similarity). .

gene.name: NPHS2 stomatin family member, podocin
gene.function: Plays a role in the regulation of glomerular permeability, acting probably as a linker between the plasma membrane and the cytoskeleton.

gene.name: Rac family small GTPase 1
gene.function: Plasma membrane-associated small GTPase which cycles between active GTP-bound and inactive GDP-bound states. In its active state, binds to a variety of effector proteins to regulate cellular responses such as secretory processes, phagocytosis of apoptotic cells, epithelial cell polarization, neurons adhesion, migration and differentiation, and growth-factor induced formation of membrane ruffles. Rac1 p21/rho GDI heterodimer is the active component of the cytosolic factor sigma 1, which is involved in stimulation of the NADPH oxidase activity in macrophages. Essential for the SPATA13- mediated regulation of cell migration and adhesion assembly and disassembly. Stimulates PKN2 kinase activity. In concert with RAB7A, plays a role in regulating the formation of RBs (ruffled borders) in osteoclasts. In podocytes, promotes nuclear shuttling of NR3C2; this modulation is required for a proper kidney functioning. Required for atypical chemokine receptor ACKR2-induced LIMK1-PAK1-dependent phosphorylation of cofilin (CFL1) and for up-regulation of ACKR2 from endosomal compartment to cell membrane, increasing its efficiency in chemokine uptake and degradation. In neurons, is involved in dendritic spine formation and synaptic plasticity (By similarity). In hippocampal neurons, involved in spine morphogenesis and synapse formation, through local activation at synapses by guanine nucleotide exchange factors (GEFs), such as ARHGEF6/ARHGEF7/PIX. In synapses, seems to mediate the regulation of F-actin cluster formation performed by SHANK3. In neurons, plays a crucial role in regulating GABA(A) receptor synaptic stability and hence GABAergic inhibitory synaptic transmission through its role in PAK1 activation and eventually F-actin stabilization (By similarity). Required for DSG3 translocation to cell-cell junctions, DSG3-mediated organization of cortical F-actin bundles and anchoring of actin at cell junctions; via interaction with DSG3. Subunit of the phagocyte NADPH oxidase complex that mediates the transfer of electrons from cytosolic NADPH to O2 to produce the superoxide anion (O2(-)).

gene.name: spalt like transcription factor 2
gene.function: Probable transcription factor that plays a role in eye development before, during, and after optic fissure closure. .

gene.name: semaphorin 3A
gene.function: Involved in the development of the olfactory system and in neuronal control of puberty. Induces the collapse and paralysis of neuronal growth cones. Could serve as a ligand that guides specific growth cones by a motility-inhibiting mechanism. Binds to the complex neuropilin-1/plexin-1. .

gene.name: shroom family member 3
gene.function: Controls cell shape changes in the neuroepithelium during neural tube closure. Induces apical constriction in epithelial cells by promoting the apical accumulation of F-actin and myosin II, and probably by bundling stress fibers (By similarity). Induces apicobasal cell elongation by redistributing gamma-tubulin and directing the assembly of robust apicobasal microtubule arrays (By similarity). .

gene.name: SMAD family member 2
gene.function: Receptor-regulated SMAD (R-SMAD) that is an intracellular signal transducer and transcriptional modulator activated by TGF-beta (transforming growth factor) and activin type 1 receptor kinases. Binds the TRE element in the promoter region of many genes that are regulated by TGF-beta and, on formation of the SMAD2/SMAD4 complex, activates transcription. Promotes TGFB1-mediated transcription of odontoblastic differentiation genes in dental papilla cells (By similarity). Positively regulates PDPK1 kinase activity by stimulating its dissociation from the 14-3-3 protein YWHAQ which acts as a negative regulator. May act as a tumor suppressor in colorectal carcinoma.

gene.name: SMAD family member 3
gene.function: Receptor-regulated SMAD (R-SMAD) that is an intracellular signal transducer and transcriptional modulator activated by TGF-beta (transforming growth factor) and activin type 1 receptor kinases. Binds the TRE element in the promoter region of many genes that are regulated by TGF-beta and, on formation of the SMAD3/SMAD4 complex, activates transcription. Also can form a SMAD3/SMAD4/JUN/FOS complex at the AP- 1/SMAD site to regulate TGF-beta-mediated transcription. Has an inhibitory effect on wound healing probably by modulating both growth and migration of primary keratinocytes and by altering the TGF-mediated chemotaxis of monocytes. This effect on wound healing appears to be hormone-sensitive. Regulator of chondrogenesis and osteogenesis and inhibits early healing of bone fractures. Positively regulates PDPK1 kinase activity by stimulating its dissociation from the 14-3-3 protein YWHAQ which acts as a negative regulator.

gene.name: SMAD family member 4
gene.function: In muscle physiology, plays a central role in the balance between atrophy and hypertrophy. When recruited by MSTN, promotes atrophy response via phosphorylated SMAD2/4. MSTN decrease causes SMAD4 release and subsequent recruitment by the BMP pathway to promote hypertrophy via phosphorylated SMAD1/5/8. Acts synergistically with SMAD1 and YY1 in bone morphogenetic protein (BMP)-mediated cardiac- specific gene expression. Binds to SMAD binding elements (SBEs) (5'- GTCT/AGAC-3') within BMP response element (BMPRE) of cardiac activating regions (By similarity). Common SMAD (co-SMAD) is the coactivator and mediator of signal transduction by TGF-beta (transforming growth factor). Component of the heterotrimeric SMAD2/SMAD3-SMAD4 complex that forms in the nucleus and is required for the TGF-mediated signaling. Promotes binding of the SMAD2/SMAD4/FAST-1 complex to DNA and provides an activation function required for SMAD1 or SMAD2 to stimulate transcription. Component of the multimeric SMAD3/SMAD4/JUN/FOS complex which forms at the AP1 promoter site; required for synergistic transcriptional activity in response to TGF- beta. May act as a tumor suppressor. Positively regulates PDPK1 kinase activity by stimulating its dissociation from the 14-3-3 protein YWHAQ which acts as a negative regulator.

gene.name: SMAD family member 7
gene.function: Antagonist of signaling by TGF-beta (transforming growth factor) type 1 receptor superfamily members; has been shown to inhibit TGF-beta (Transforming growth factor) and activin signaling by associating with their receptors thus preventing SMAD2 access. Functions as an adapter to recruit SMURF2 to the TGF-beta receptor complex. Also acts by recruiting the PPP1R15A-PP1 complex to TGFBR1, which promotes its dephosphorylation. Positively regulates PDPK1 kinase activity by stimulating its dissociation from the 14-3-3 protein YWHAQ which acts as a negative regulator.

gene.name: secreted protein acidic and cysteine rich
gene.function: Appears to regulate cell growth through interactions with the extracellular matrix and cytokines. Binds calcium and copper, several types of collagen, albumin, thrombospondin, PDGF and cell membranes. There are two calcium binding sites; an acidic domain that binds 5 to 8 Ca(2+) with a low affinity and an EF-hand loop that binds a Ca(2+) ion with a high affinity.

gene.name: serine/threonine kinase 11
gene.function: Tumor suppressor serine/threonine-protein kinase that controls the activity of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) family members, thereby playing a role in various processes such as cell metabolism, cell polarity, apoptosis and DNA damage response. Acts by phosphorylating the T-loop of AMPK family proteins, thus promoting their activity: phosphorylates PRKAA1, PRKAA2, BRSK1, BRSK2, MARK1, MARK2, MARK3, MARK4, NUAK1, NUAK2, SIK1, SIK2, SIK3 and SNRK but not MELK. Also phosphorylates non-AMPK family proteins such as STRADA, PTEN and possibly p53/TP53. Acts as a key upstream regulator of AMPK by mediating phosphorylation and activation of AMPK catalytic subunits PRKAA1 and PRKAA2 and thereby regulates processes including: inhibition of signaling pathways that promote cell growth and proliferation when energy levels are low, glucose homeostasis in liver, activation of autophagy when cells undergo nutrient deprivation, and B- cell differentiation in the germinal center in response to DNA damage. Also acts as a regulator of cellular polarity by remodeling the actin cytoskeleton. Required for cortical neuron polarization by mediating phosphorylation and activation of BRSK1 and BRSK2, leading to axon initiation and specification. Involved in DNA damage response: interacts with p53/TP53 and recruited to the CDKN1A/WAF1 promoter to participate in transcription activation. Able to phosphorylate p53/TP53; the relevance of such result in vivo is however unclear and phosphorylation may be indirect and mediated by downstream STK11/LKB1 kinase NUAK1. Also acts as a mediator of p53/TP53-dependent apoptosis via interaction with p53/TP53: translocates to the mitochondrion during apoptosis and regulates p53/TP53-dependent apoptosis pathways. Regulates UV radiation-induced DNA damage response mediated by CDKN1A. In association with NUAK1, phosphorylates CDKN1A in response to UV radiation and contributes to its degradation which is necessary for optimal DNA repair.

gene.name: TAR DNA binding protein
gene.function: RNA-binding protein that is involved in various steps of RNA biogenesis and processing. Preferentially binds, via its two RNA recognition motifs RRM1 and RRM2, to GU-repeats on RNA molecules predominantly localized within long introns and in the 3'UTR of mRNAs. In turn, regulates the splicing of many non-coding and protein-coding RNAs including proteins involved in neuronal survival, as well as mRNAs that encode proteins relevant for neurodegenerative diseases. Plays a role in maintaining mitochondrial homeostasis by regulating the processing of mitochondrial transcripts. Also regulates mRNA stability by recruiting CNOT7/CAF1 deadenylase on mRNA 3'UTR leading to poly(A) tail deadenylation and thus shortening. In response to oxidative insult, associates with stalled ribosomes localized to stress granules (SGs) and contributes to cell survival. Also participates in the normal skeletal muscle formation and regeneration, forming cytoplasmic myo-granules and binding mRNAs that encode sarcomeric proteins. Plays a role in the maintenance of the circadian clock periodicity via stabilization of the CRY1 and CRY2 proteins in a FBXL3-dependent manner. Negatively regulates the expression of CDK6. Regulates the expression of HDAC6, ATG7 and VCP in a PPIA/CYPA-dependent manner.

gene.name: TIMP metallopeptidase inhibitor 1
gene.function: Metalloproteinase inhibitor that functions by forming one to one complexes with target metalloproteinases, such as collagenases, and irreversibly inactivates them by binding to their catalytic zinc cofactor. Acts on MMP1, MMP2, MMP3, MMP7, MMP8, MMP9, MMP10, MMP11, MMP12, MMP13 and MMP16. Does not act on MMP14. Also functions as a growth factor that regulates cell differentiation, migration and cell death and activates cellular signaling cascades via CD63 and ITGB1. Plays a role in integrin signaling. Mediates erythropoiesis in vitro; but, unlike IL3, it is species-specific, stimulating the growth and differentiation of only human and murine erythroid progenitors.

gene.name: tumor protein p53
gene.function: Multifunctional transcription factor that induces cell cycle arrest, DNA repair or apoptosis upon binding to its target DNA sequence. Acts as a tumor suppressor in many tumor types; induces growth arrest or apoptosis depending on the physiological circumstances and cell type. Negatively regulates cell division by controlling expression of a set of genes required for this process. One of the activated genes is an inhibitor of cyclin-dependent kinases. Apoptosis induction seems to be mediated either by stimulation of BAX and FAS antigen expression, or by repression of Bcl-2 expression. Its pro-apoptotic activity is activated via its interaction with PPP1R13B/ASPP1 or TP53BP2/ASPP2. However, this activity is inhibited when the interaction with PPP1R13B/ASPP1 or TP53BP2/ASPP2 is displaced by PPP1R13L/iASPP. In cooperation with mitochondrial PPIF is involved in activating oxidative stress-induced necrosis; the function is largely independent of transcription. Induces the transcription of long intergenic non-coding RNA p21 (lincRNA-p21) and lincRNA-Mkln1. LincRNA-p21 participates in TP53-dependent transcriptional repression leading to apoptosis and seems to have an effect on cell-cycle regulation. Implicated in Notch signaling cross-over. Prevents CDK7 kinase activity when associated to CAK complex in response to DNA damage, thus stopping cell cycle progression. Isoform 2 enhances the transactivation activity of isoform 1 from some but not all TP53-inducible promoters. Isoform 4 suppresses transactivation activity and impairs growth suppression mediated by isoform 1. Isoform 7 inhibits isoform 1-mediated apoptosis. Regulates the circadian clock by repressing CLOCK-BMAL1-mediated transcriptional activation of PER2.

gene.name: transient receptor potential cation channel subfamily C member 5
gene.function: Forms a receptor-activated non-selective calcium permeant cation channel. Mediates calcium-dependent phosphatidylserine externalization and apoptosis in neurons via its association with PLSCR1 (By similarity). Acts on distinct neuronal populations in the hypothalamus to regulate innate behaviors including feeding, anxiety (flight/fight/fear), socialization, and maternal care (By similarity).

gene.name: ubiquitin specific peptidase 46
gene.function: Deubiquitinating enzyme that plays a role in behavior, possibly by regulating GABA action. May act by mediating the deubiquitination of GAD1/GAD67 (By similarity). Has almost no deubiquitinating activity by itself and requires the interaction with WDR48 to have a high activity. Not involved in deubiquitination of monoubiquitinated FANCD2.

An anomaly of podocyte morphology characterized by the loss of the interdigitating foot process pattern (generally called foot process effacement; FPE). The term FPE designates the loss of the usual interdigitating pattern of foot processes of neighboring podocytes, leading to relatively broad expanses of podocyte processes covering the glomerular basement membrane (GBM). It is widely viewed as a pathological derangement that is associated with leakage of macromolecules such as albumin through the glomerular filtration barrier.

Cysts of the cortex of the kidney.

papers.title: Organoprotective Effects of Spironolactone on Top of Ramipril Therapy in a Mouse Model for Alport Syndrome.
papers.summary: In COL4A3−/− mice with Alport syndrome, adding spironolactone to ramipril better preserved renal function, reduced proteinuria and matrix accumulation, and reduced glomerular and tubulointerstitial fibrosis than ramipril monotherapy. The improved renal outcomes did not extend lifespan, and treatment was associated with increased male body weight and possible hyperkalemia-related premature death.
papers.why: The Alport mouse-model study directly shows that adding spironolactone to ramipril reduces proteinuria and fibrosis, although it does not improve survival and carries hyperkalemia risk.

papers.title: Systematic Review of Management Strategies for Alport Syndrome: Implications for Male Patients.
papers.summary: This systematic review finds preliminary clinical evidence that bardoxolone methyl, ramipril, and losartan may slow renal deterioration in Alport syndrome, with earlier treatment appearing more beneficial. Evidence remains limited by small trials, heterogeneity, biased reporting and dropout in one study, and uncertainty about long-term effects and applicability across genetically and geographically diverse populations.
papers.why: This systematic review evaluates existing Alport syndrome management strategies and reports potential renal-protective effects for bardoxolone methyl, ramipril, and losartan.

papers.title: From RAAS blockade to regenerative medicine: evolving treatment strategies in Alport syndrome.
papers.summary: This review describes Alport syndrome as a COL4A3-, COL4A4-, or COL4A5-associated hereditary glomerulopathy and reviews standard, investigational, genetic, metabolic, mitochondrial, and regenerative treatment strategies. It reports encouraging preclinical results for several interventions, especially empagliflozin, lipid-handling agents, mitochondrial modulation, exon skipping, and stem cells, while emphasizing that most disease-modifying approaches remain investigational and have important delivery, safety, or efficacy limitations.
papers.why: Reviews established, clinical-trial, and preclinical treatment strategies directly applicable to Alport syndrome, including kidney-protective drugs and disease-modifying genetic and regenerative approaches.

papers.title: A multidrug, antiproteinuric approach to alport syndrome: a ten-year cohort study.
papers.summary: In a prospective off-on-off cohort study of nine adults with albuminuric Alport syndrome, the multidrug Remission Clinic regimen reduced albuminuria, blood pressure, serum lipids, and albumin/IgG fractional clearances during treatment, while these proteinuria and clearance effects returned toward baseline after withdrawal. During long-term follow-up, seven of eight actively followed patients retained normal renal function, whereas one patient with severe baseline renal insufficiency progressed to end-stage renal disease; interpretation is limited by the small, uncontrolled cohort.
papers.why: A prospective cohort directly showed that combined ACE inhibition, angiotensin-receptor blockade, diltiazem, and fluvastatin substantially reduced albuminuria in adults with Alport syndrome.

papers.title: Hydroxychloroquine Ameliorates Hematuria in Children with X-Linked Alport Syndrome: Retrospective Case Series Study.
papers.summary: In a retrospective case series of eight children with X-linked Alport syndrome, hydroxychloroquine added to benazepril was associated with reduced hematuria in all patients and reduced proteinuria in five patients after six months, without severe adverse events. The findings provide only preliminary evidence because the study was retrospective, small, used an imprecise proteinuria assay, and does not establish a causal inflammatory mechanism or long-term renal benefit.
papers.why: This retrospective series directly reports hydroxychloroquine treatment in children with X-linked Alport syndrome and shows reduced hematuria and, in several children, proteinuria.

papers.title: Anti-microRNA-21 Therapy on Top of ACE Inhibition Delays Renal Failure in Alport Syndrome Mouse Models.
papers.summary: In two Col4a3-null mouse models of Alport syndrome, adding the anti-miR-21 oligonucleotide lademirsen to ramipril improved renal pathology and kidney function and prolonged survival, with additive effects most evident in the rapidly progressing 129/SvJ model. Transcriptomic analysis showed that lademirsen particularly normalized profibrotic renal tubulointerstitial injury pathways, but its effects on established disease and the molecular response to combination therapy remain incompletely resolved.
papers.why: The anti-miR-21 treatment reduced fibrosis and proteinuria and improved kidney function and survival when added to ACE inhibition in Alport mouse models.

papers.title: Dual inhibition of the endothelin and angiotensin receptor ameliorates renal and inner ear pathologies in Alport mice.
papers.summary: In an autosomal-recessive Col4a3 knockout mouse model of Alport syndrome, dual endothelin type-A and angiotensin II type-1 receptor inhibition with sparsentan improved renal pathology, preserved glomerular filtration rate, delayed proteinuria, and extended lifespan. Sparsentan also reduced strial capillary basement-membrane pathology and protected against noise-induced hearing loss, whereas losartan improved several renal outcomes but did not improve hearing recovery.
papers.why: Sparsentan improved renal function, proteinuria, fibrosis, lifespan, and inner-ear pathology in an Alport mouse model, outperforming losartan for several outcomes.

papers.title: Rare hereditary COL4A3/COL4A4 variants may be mistaken for familial focal segmental glomerulosclerosis.
papers.summary: In seven of 70 families referred with familial focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, rare or novel COL4A3 or COL4A4 variants segregated with nephrotic-range proteinuria, hematuria, and FSGS, showing that collagen IV–related disease can phenocopy familial FSGS. The findings support screening and molecular reclassification of familial FSGS cases with next-generation sequencing, while classical Alport glomerular basement membrane changes and post-transplant disease recurrence were absent in the evaluated families.
papers.why: The study shows that sequencing COL4A3 and COL4A4 identifies Alport-related disease in families otherwise classified as hereditary FSGS.

papers.title: Consensus statement on standards and guidelines for the molecular diagnostics of Alport syndrome: refining the ACMG criteria.
papers.summary: This consensus statement expands molecular testing for Alport syndrome beyond classic disease to proteinuria, steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome, FSGS, familial IgA glomerulonephritis, and unexplained end-stage kidney failure, particularly through sequencing of COL4A3–COL4A5. It provides variant interpretation guidance, emphasizes genotype-specific functional evidence and splicing confirmation, and highlights hypomorphic collagen IV variants that can cause milder or later-onset disease.
papers.why: This consensus statement directly refines molecular diagnostic standards and variant interpretation for Alport syndrome.

papers.title: Natural History and Genotype-Phenotype Correlation in Female X-Linked Alport Syndrome.
papers.summary: This Japanese retrospective cohort study shows that female X-linked Alport syndrome can be severe despite a median age of 65 years at end-stage renal disease, with proteinuria appearing at a median age of 7 years. COL4A5 genotype did not predict renal severity, and sequencing of 45 podocyte-related genes found no plausible modifier variants in 23 of 24 clinically severe cases.
papers.why: The large female X-linked Alport cohort provides natural-history measures of proteinuria onset, renal survival, and ESRD that can support prognostic studies and trial endpoints.

papers.title: Clinical genetic testing using a custom-designed steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome gene panel: analysis and recommendations.
papers.summary: A targeted 37-gene next-generation sequencing panel that detects single-nucleotide variants and copy number variants provided a likely genetic diagnosis in 17 of 35 patients referred with suspected Alport syndrome, with all pathogenic variants found in COL4A3, COL4A4, or COL4A5. The study supports early clinical gene-panel testing and orthogonal confirmation of detected copy number variants.
papers.why: The custom NGS panel produced a likely genetic diagnosis in 17 of 35 patients with hematuria or suspected Alport syndrome and supports early clinical genetic testing.

papers.title: Discoidin domain receptor 1 activation links extracellular matrix to podocyte lipotoxicity in Alport syndrome.
papers.summary: The paper identifies a collagen I–DDR1–CD36 pathway that increases free-fatty-acid uptake, triglyceride accumulation, and podocyte injury in Alport syndrome models. Ezetimibe disrupts DDR1–CD36 interaction and improves renal function, fibrosis, lipid accumulation, and glomerular ultrastructure in Col4a3 knockout mice to an extent similar to ramipril, but its clinical efficacy remains unestablished.
papers.why: Directly demonstrates in an Alport mouse model that ezetimibe disrupts the CD36/DDR1 interaction, reduces podocyte lipotoxicity, and preserves renal function.

papers.title: Targeted exome sequencing integrated with clinicopathological information reveals novel and rare mutations in atypical, suspected and unknown cases of Alport syndrome or proteinuria.
papers.summary: Targeted exome sequencing identified compound-heterozygous COL4A3 variants that, together with characteristic pathology and progressive sensorineural hearing loss, established atypical Alport syndrome in a patient with concurrent vesicoureteral reflux and a focal segmental glomerulosclerosis biopsy pattern. A multiplexed 19-gene assay also recovered known or novel COL4A3, COL4A4, or COL4A5 variants in patients with established or equivocal Alport syndrome and identified APOL1 and LAMA5 variants in focal segmental glomerulosclerosis cases.
papers.why: Targeted exome sequencing combined with clinicopathologic information successfully diagnosed atypical or genetically unresolved Alport syndrome and proteinuria.

papers.title: Genotype-phenotype correlations for COL4A3-COL4A5 variants resulting in Gly substitutions in Alport syndrome.
papers.summary: This observational genotype–phenotype study shows that the identity and collagenous location of Gly substitutions in COL4A3, COL4A4, and COL4A5 help stratify Alport syndrome severity. Highly destabilising substitutions are associated with earlier kidney failure and hearing-loss diagnosis, whereas substitutions adjacent to non-collagenous boundaries are associated with delayed kidney failure and reduced haematuria risk, although these features explain only a small proportion of haematuria risk.
papers.why: COL4A3, COL4A4, and COL4A5 glycine-substitution characteristics were quantitatively associated with hematuria, age at kidney failure, and hearing-loss timing.

papers.title: Diagnosis, management and treatment of the Alport syndrome - 2024 guideline on behalf of ERKNet, ERA and ESPN.
papers.summary: This guideline concludes that Alport syndrome is a heterogeneous COL4A3, COL4A4, or COL4A5 glomerulopathy for which joint genetic analysis is the key diagnostic test. Early renin-angiotensin system blockade is the standard nephroprotective treatment, while SGLT2 inhibitors may be added in selected adults, although direct trial evidence in Alport syndrome remains limited and a mouse study found no significant kidney-failure benefit from empagliflozin.
papers.why: This disease-specific guideline provides evidence-graded diagnostic and management approaches for Alport syndrome.

papers.title: Genotype-phenotype correlations and nephroprotective effects of RAAS inhibition in patients with autosomal recessive Alport syndrome.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 101 patients with autosomal recessive Alport syndrome, RAAS inhibition was associated with reduced risk and delayed onset of stage 5 chronic kidney disease, especially when initiated earlier. Disease severity and kidney-function decline were greater in patients without missense variants, while genetic testing and glomerular basement membrane electron microscopy were supported as key diagnostic approaches.
papers.why: A 101-patient study provides evidence that early RAAS inhibition delays kidney failure in autosomal recessive Alport syndrome and links genotype to treatment response.

papers.title: A mouse Col4a4 mutation causing Alport glomerulosclerosis with abnormal collagen α3α4α5(IV) trimers.
papers.summary: The study identifies a spontaneous Col4a4bwk splice-donor mutation that produces a novel mouse model of rapidly progressive Alport syndrome, with glomerulosclerosis, abnormal glomerular basement membrane architecture, and end-stage renal disease. Mutant mice retain secreted, partially assembled collagen α3α4α5(IV) trimers in the glomerular basement membrane, while genetic background strongly modifies albuminuria and disease progression.
papers.why: The bwk mouse develops Alport-type glomerular basement-membrane abnormalities and kidney disease while supporting testing of therapies and modifier genes.

papers.title: New frontiers to cure Alport syndrome: COL4A3 and COL4A5 gene editing in podocyte-lineage cells.
papers.summary: The paper demonstrates a variant-specific, self-inactivating dual-plasmid CRISPR/Cas9 strategy in urine-derived podocyte-lineage cells from two patients with Alport syndrome. It restored wild-type sequence at COL4A5 p.(Gly624Asp) and COL4A3 p.(Gly856Glu) with 58.8% and 44.2% homology-directed repair, respectively, with comparatively few undesired insertions/deletions, but the work remains an in vitro proof of concept.
papers.why: CRISPR/Cas9 editing reverted more than 40% of tested pathogenic COL4A3 and COL4A5 variants in patient-derived podocyte-lineage models.

papers.title: The 2014International Workshop on Alport Syndrome.
papers.summary: This workshop report summarizes mechanistic findings and candidate research solutions for Alport syndrome, emphasizing defective collagen IV networks in the glomerular basement membrane, podocyte injury, and fibrosis. It reports proof-of-principle rescue in Col4a3−/− mice, mixed findings for fibrosis attenuation, and proposed or experimentally investigated approaches including collagen-network restoration, focal adhesion kinase and receptor inhibition, stem-cell infusion, microRNA-21 targeting, and improved molecular diagnostics.
papers.why: The workshop report states that ACE inhibition slows progression to ESRD in Alport syndrome and documents an international research and stakeholder collaboration.

papers.title: Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 Inhibitors in Patients with Hereditary Podocytopathies, Alport Syndrome, and FSGS: A Case Series to Better Plan a Large-Scale Study.
papers.summary: This six-patient observational case series found that sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors, added to renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system blockade in most patients, were generally well tolerated and reduced albuminuria in Alport syndrome, although individual proteinuria responses were variable. Kidney function remained broadly stable across the cohort, but an initial eGFR decline in one patient and the small, uncontrolled study prevent causal conclusions and require confirmation in randomized trials.
papers.why: This first case series reports treatment and kidney-function data for SGLT2 inhibitors in patients with Alport syndrome, including an approximately 40% reduction in albuminuria.

papers.title: The role of molecular genetics in diagnosing familial hematuria(s).
papers.summary: This review shows that Alport syndrome and related hereditary hematurias can be distinguished by molecular testing for pathogenic COL4A3, COL4A4, COL4A5, or CFHR5 variants, complemented by kidney biopsy with electron microscopy. It also emphasizes that apparently mild or benign hematuria syndromes can progress to proteinuria, chronic kidney disease, and end-stage kidney disease, particularly in certain COL4 mutation-bearing families.
papers.why: The review establishes collagen IV molecular testing as a definitive diagnostic approach for Alport syndrome and related familial hematuria and notes that it can sometimes obviate renal biopsy.

papers.title: Last Nucleotide Substitutions of COL4A5 Exons Cause Aberrant Splicing.
papers.summary: Functional testing showed that 17 of 20 single-base substitutions at the last nucleotide position of COL4A5 exons caused aberrant splicing rather than missense effects, with three available patient transcripts confirming the minigene results. Male patients with XLAS carrying these splicing variants developed ESKD earlier than patients with missense variants, supporting mRNA analysis for variant classification and kidney-prognosis prediction.
papers.why: The study shows through functional assays and patient transcripts that 85% of tested COL4A5 last-nucleotide substitutions disrupt splicing, improving molecular diagnosis and prognosis.

papers.title: Angiotensin-[1-7] attenuates kidney injury in experimental Alport syndrome.
papers.summary: Continuous infusion of angiotensin-[1–7] attenuated renal fibrosis, inflammation, oxidative stress, apoptosis, and glomerulosclerosis in male Col4a3−/− mice, while also protecting TGF-β–stimulated HK-2 human proximal tubular epithelial cells. Treatment was associated with reduced TGF-β/Smad and MAPK signaling and restoration of the kidney ACE2/angiotensin-[1–7]/Mas receptor axis, but no clinical treatment efficacy was evaluated and blood pressure, blood angiotensin-[1–7], and kidney angiotensin-[1–7] were not measured.
papers.why: Angiotensin-[1-7] reduced fibrosis, inflammation, apoptosis and TGF-beta/Smad signaling in Col4a3-deficient mice and human kidney cells, directly demonstrating a renoprotective intervention in experimental Alport syndrome.

papers.title: The Contribution of COL4A5 Splicing Variants to the Pathogenesis of X-Linked Alport Syndrome.
papers.summary: This review reports that pathogenic COL4A5 splicing variants, including deep intronic and exonic variants, account for a substantial proportion of X-linked Alport syndrome and can alter kidney prognosis according to the resulting in-frame or out-of-frame transcript. It describes transcript-based diagnostic strategies and reports that an antisense oligonucleotide improved clinical and pathological outcomes in a male XLAS model mouse, while disease-specific splicing therapies remain investigational.
papers.why: Although it is a review, it describes validated molecular approaches for detecting COL4A5 splicing defects and specific therapeutic strategies for controlling aberrant splicing.

papers.title: A Systematic Review of Pathogenic COL4A5 Variants and Proteinuria in Women and Girls With X-linked Alport Syndrome.
papers.summary: The systematic review found that proteinuria marks disease severity and progression in women and girls with X-linked Alport syndrome, with truncating, large, or splicing COL4A5 variants associated with earlier proteinuria detection than missense variants. COL4A5 genotype correlated with proteinuria but not with age at kidney failure, and proteinuria detected before age 15 was associated with more rapid progression to kidney failure.
papers.why: A systematic review of 366 women and girls with X-linked Alport syndrome shows that proteinuria and variant class correlate with kidney failure risk, supporting proteinuria as a prognostic outcome measure.

papers.title: X-linked Alport syndrome: pathogenic variant features and further auditory genotype-phenotype correlations in males.
papers.summary: In 87 males with X-linked Alport syndrome, hearing loss was bilateral, symmetrical, sensorineural, and age-associated; 63.2% had hearing loss, and 92.73% of affected patients had a groove-type audiometric curve. COL4A5 pathogenic variant class was associated with hearing-loss frequency, severity, and age of onset, while variant position along the gene and the rate of progression after hearing loss began were not significantly associated with the auditory phenotype.
papers.why: The study provides longitudinal audiological outcome measures and genotype-phenotype correlations for hearing loss in male X-linked Alport syndrome.

papers.title: Metformin ameliorates the severity of experimental Alport syndrome.
papers.summary: In mouse models, metformin reduced proteinuria, glomerular injury, renal inflammation, fibrosis, podocyte loss, and glomerular metabolic dysregulation in Alport syndrome, while increasing AMPK, ERK, p53, and NRF2 signaling. Metformin also prolonged survival in selected Alport models and reduced proteinuria and glomerular injury in adriamycin-induced nephropathy, but the standard-dose combination with losartan caused acute toxicity.
papers.why: Metformin reduced proteinuria, inflammation, fibrosis, and glomerular injury and extended lifespan in experimental Alport syndrome.

papers.title: Genotype and Outcome After Kidney Transplantation in Alport Syndrome.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 73 genetically confirmed patients with Alport syndrome receiving 93 kidney grafts, mutation severity was associated with earlier end-stage renal disease and more acute rejection but not with patient or graft survival. Clinically significant de novo anti-GBM glomerulonephritis was uncommon, occurring in one patient with a severe COL4A5 mutation and recurring in a subsequent graft.
papers.why: A 73-patient, 93-graft cohort demonstrates kidney transplantation outcomes in Alport syndrome and quantifies recurrent anti-GBM glomerulonephritis risk.

papers.title: Renal transplantation in patients with Alport syndrome: patient selection, outcomes, and donor evaluation.
papers.summary: This review reports generally excellent patient and graft survival after kidney transplantation for Alport syndrome, with preemptive transplantation preferred for patients approaching end-stage renal disease. It also identifies posttransplant anti-GBM nephritis as a rare, potentially devastating complication, emphasizes genotype-based evaluation of related donors, and notes that proposed anti-GBM antibody monitoring has not been shown to improve diagnosis or outcomes.
papers.why: The paper reports renal transplantation as an established treatment for Alport syndrome and describes outcomes, donor-selection considerations, and the key post-transplant complication.

papers.title: SGLT2-Inhibition in Patients With Alport Syndrome.
papers.summary: In this observational multicenter cohort of 112 patients with Alport syndrome, SGLT2 inhibition—mostly dapagliflozin—was associated with a significant reduction in albuminuria over approximately 3–15 months, usually alongside renin-angiotensin system inhibition. Estimated GFR declined, and a small number of severe adverse events occurred; because the study was uncontrolled and retrospective data were included, whether albuminuria reduction translates into delayed kidney failure or long-term kidney protection remains uncertain.
papers.why: An international observational cohort of 112 patients with Alport syndrome found that SGLT2 inhibition reduced albuminuria when added to renin-angiotensin system blockade.

papers.title: Trimerization and Genotype-Phenotype Correlation of COL4A5 Mutants in Alport Syndrome.
papers.summary: The study shows that COL4A5 glycine-substituted missense mutants associated with severe Alport syndrome generally have reduced α345(IV) trimer secretion, whereas mutants associated with milder disease retain activity closer to wild type. A split nanoluciferase assay in transfected HEK293T cells largely correlated with clinical severity, but it could not predict severity with 100% accuracy.
papers.why: A cell-based assay quantified collagen IV alpha345 heterotrimer formation and secretion for nine COL4A5 mutants and correlated these measurements with clinical severity.

papers.title: NanoLuc reporters identify COL4A5 nonsense mutations susceptible to drug-induced stop codon readthrough.
papers.summary: The study shows that drug-induced premature termination codon readthrough restored full-length COL4A5 production for a subset of nonsense variants associated with X-linked Alport syndrome and was observed ex vivo in Col4a5-R1563X mouse kidney cells. Variant-specific screening, functional heterotrimer assays, and enhancer testing identified candidate readthrough approaches, but efficacy in vivo, long-term toxicity, and clinical benefit remain unestablished.
papers.why: The study tests readthrough drugs and functional NanoLuc assays for Alport-causing COL4A5 nonsense variants, including validation in engineered kidney cells.

papers.title: Effect of heterozygous pathogenic COL4A3 or COL4A4 variants on patients with X-linked Alport syndrome.
papers.summary: In a small observational cohort, children with X-linked Alport syndrome carrying an additional heterozygous pathogenic COL4A3 or COL4A4 variant had more severe proteinuria than males with a single pathogenic COL4A5 variant. The study also identified a rare three-gene genotype and supports sequencing all three major Alport genes with targeted next-generation sequencing for diagnosis and genetic counseling.
papers.why: The study directly characterizes compound COL4A3-5 genotypes in Alport syndrome and shows how targeted sequencing informs disease severity and prognosis.

papers.title: Heterozygous COL4A3 Variants in Histologically Diagnosed Focal Segmental Glomerulosclerosis.
papers.summary: This case report identifies compound-heterozygous missense variants in COL4A3, including the novel p.Gly631Val variant, in a woman whose nephrotic-range proteinuria and biopsy initially suggested hereditary focal segmental glomerulosclerosis. Re-examination of glomerular basement membrane ultrastructure and molecular genetic testing led to a diagnosis of Alport syndrome, while immunosuppressive therapy failed to adequately reduce proteinuria and molecular testing may help avoid unnecessary immunosuppression.
papers.why: The case shows that targeted collagen IV genetic testing and ultrastructural kidney analysis can diagnose Alport syndrome presenting atypically as FSGS.

papers.title: Increased prevalence of kidney cysts in individuals carrying heterozygous COL4A3 or COL4A4 pathogenic variants.
papers.summary: In 157 adults with heterozygous COL4A3 or COL4A4 pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants, kidney ultrasound identified kidney cysts more frequently than in a sex- and age-matched general population. Cyst prevalence increased with older age and lower eGFR, but was not independently associated with proteinuria, sex, or causative gene, and cystic nephromegaly was uncommon and clinically negligible.
papers.why: The multicenter study identifies simple kidney cysts as an imaging phenotype associated with COL4A3/COL4A4-related Alport disease and relates cyst presence to age and eGFR.

papers.title: Creation of X-linked Alport syndrome rat model with Col4a5 deficiency.
papers.summary: The paper created a novel X-linked Alport syndrome model by generating Col4a5-deficient WKY rats with rGONAD genome editing. The rats developed progressive kidney dysfunction, glomerular basement membrane abnormalities, fibrosis, disrupted type IV collagen networks, and increased renal disease-associated proteins, supporting their use for mechanistic and therapeutic studies.
papers.why: The new rat reproduces hematuria, proteinuria, renal failure, fibrosis, and collagen-chain abnormalities characteristic of Alport syndrome.

papers.title: A novel nanoluciferase transgenic reporter measures proteinuria in zebrafish.
papers.summary: The paper develops the liver-specific NL-D3 nanoluciferase transgenic zebrafish as a quantitative, high-throughput proteinuria reporter for proximal-tubular and glomerular dysfunction. CRISPR-Cas9 depletion of col4a3 or col4a4 creates an early-stage Alport syndrome model with thickened glomerular basement membranes, podocyte effacement, and proteinuria; captopril almost completely prevents the proteinuria, whereas 2,3-BDM partially reduces it.
papers.why: The NL-D3 reporter quantifies proteinuria in Col4a4-deficient Alport zebrafish, validates captopril response, and enables high-throughput screening for disease-modifying drugs.

papers.title: Non-collagen genes role in digenic Alport syndrome.
papers.summary: The paper identifies hypomorphic LAMA5 variants co-segregating with pathogenic COL4A4 or COL4A5 variants in three families with a likely digenic form of Alport syndrome. It proposes an NPHS2 variant as an additional possible modifier and recommends broadened next-generation sequencing to characterize non-collagen contributors, clinical severity, and recurrence risk.
papers.why: The study provides same-disease genetic testing data identifying LAMA5 and NPHS2 variants as modifiers and supporting broader genomic panels for suspected digenic Alport syndrome.

papers.title: Endoplasmic reticulum stress and proteasome pathway involvement in human podocyte injury with a truncated COL4A3 mutation.
papers.summary: The paper shows that severe NC1-truncated COL4A3 mutations increase endoplasmic reticulum stress and apoptosis in human and mouse podocyte models, whereas the tested missense mutations do not produce comparable changes. Proteasome inhibition with MG132 restored truncated COL4A3 expression and reduced stress- and apoptosis-related proteins, supporting a preclinical proteasome-directed approach for COL4A3-related nephropathy, including Alport syndrome.
papers.why: The paper directly shows in COL4A3-mutant podocytes that proteasome inhibition with MG132 reduces excessive endoplasmic-reticulum stress and apoptosis, while also supplying disease-relevant models.

papers.title: A Comparative Presentation of Mouse Models That Recapitulate Most Features of Alport Syndrome.
papers.summary: This review compares 15 genetically altered mouse models of Alport syndrome and shows that they reproduce many human disease features, including glomerular basement membrane abnormalities, proteinuria, kidney dysfunction, fibrosis, and variable hearing or ocular defects. It emphasizes that mutation type and genetic background strongly determine phenotype, disease onset, tissue of origin, and lifespan, while highlighting kidney injury molecule-1 and monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 as candidate biomarkers and ACE inhibitors as an existing therapeutic approach.
papers.why: This review identifies and compares existing mouse models that reproduce major Alport phenotypes and can be reused for mechanism and treatment studies.

papers.title: Molecular testing for adult type Alport syndrome.
papers.summary: The paper reports that three COL4A5 variants—C1564S, L1649R, and R1677Q—account for a large proportion of adult-type X-linked Alport syndrome mutations in the United States. A fluorescence hybridization-probe assay with melting-curve analysis accurately detected these variants in DNA samples, but had an estimated clinical sensitivity of only about 75% because it did not detect other Alport syndrome mutations.
papers.why: The study validates a targeted molecular assay for common adult-type X-linked Alport syndrome variants with high analytical performance for diagnosis and carrier testing.

papers.title: Kidney Injury by Variants in the COL4A5 Gene Aggravated by Polymorphisms in Slit Diaphragm Genes Causes Focal Segmental Glomerulosclerosis.
papers.summary: In three families with COL4A5 variants, nephrin and podocin polymorphisms were associated with unusually severe glomerular injury, including early focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, glomerular basement membrane ruptures, proteinuria, and early renal failure. The cases support a gene-interaction model in which basement membrane defects and slit diaphragm variants jointly increase podocyte vulnerability, while ramipril reduced proteinuria in one toddler.
papers.why: The study provides genetic-testing evidence that nephrin and podocin variants modify COL4A5-associated kidney injury and can inform prognosis in hereditary glomerular disease.

papers.title: The Hypomorphic Variant p.(Gly624Asp) in COL4A5 as a Possible Cause for an Unexpected Severe Phenotype in a Family With X-Linked Alport Syndrome.
papers.summary: This case report identifies the homozygous COL4A5 c.1871G>A, p.(Gly624Asp) variant in a woman with X-linked Alport syndrome and heterozygous or hemizygous states in affected relatives. The family had later-onset microscopic hematuria, microalbuminuria or proteinuria, with end-stage renal disease in affected adult males, suggesting that the variant may be more severe than previously characterized despite lacking detected additional monogenic or modifier variants.
papers.why: This case series directly characterizes a COL4A5 variant with unexpectedly severe Alport disease using molecular diagnostics and longitudinal clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Efficient Targeted Next Generation Sequencing-Based Workflow for Differential Diagnosis of Alport-Related Disorders.
papers.summary: The study demonstrates an amplicon-based next generation sequencing workflow for simultaneously testing COL4A3, COL4A4, and COL4A5 in 17 Hungarian cases with Alport syndrome or familial benign haematuria. The workflow identified causative mutations in all investigated cases, including 14 previously unpublished variants, and supported differential diagnosis, inheritance-pattern classification, and genetic counseling.
papers.why: The study successfully diagnoses Alport-related disorders using a simultaneous targeted NGS workflow and shows that molecular confirmation can obviate renal biopsy.

papers.title: An overview of the multi-pronged approach in the diagnosis of Alport syndrome for 22 children in Northeast China.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 22 children, a multi-pronged approach combining the 2015 Japanese diagnostic criteria with clinical, renal pathology, and genetic findings diagnosed more Alport syndrome cases than the 1988 criteria. The paper also documents collagen IV gene variants, characteristic glomerular basement membrane findings, variable early renal and auditory phenotypes, and reviewed or case-supported approaches to slowing renal progression.
papers.why: The study demonstrates a combined clinical, family-history, biopsy, and genotype strategy that diagnosed 22 pediatric Alport syndrome cases.

papers.title: Type IV Collagen Variants in CKD: Performance of Computational Predictions for Identifying Pathogenic Variants.
papers.summary: This paper evaluates 12 in silico prediction programs for classifying rare missense variants in COL4A3, COL4A4, and COL4A5, including variants from an FSGS cohort and public variant databases containing Alport syndrome classifications. Computational predictions were sensitive but insufficiently specific, overestimating the effects of some benign and uncertain-significance variants; split-luciferase testing identified secretory defects in all tested pathogenic COL4A3 and COL4A5 variants in the FSGS cohort but not in most variants of uncertain significance.
papers.why: The study benchmarks 12 computational predictors against curated and functionally characterized type IV collagen variants and identifies their diagnostic limitations.

papers.title: Mutation Analysis of Thin Basement Membrane Nephropathy.
papers.summary: In 13 patients with thin basement membrane nephropathy, sequencing identified heterozygous COL4A3 or COL4A4 variants in 9 patients, with 7 patients receiving pathogenic or likely pathogenic classifications under ACMG guidelines. The findings support a continuous disease spectrum from thin basement membrane nephropathy to autosomal dominant Alport syndrome and show that Sanger-negative cases can yield additional variants by exome sequencing, although MLPA detected no large copy-number variants in the four patients tested.
papers.why: The study tests a three-tier genetic diagnostic strategy in thin basement membrane nephropathy and identifies variants spanning thin basement membrane disease, FSGS, and autosomal dominant Alport syndrome.

papers.title: Slowly progressive autosomal dominant Alport Syndrome due to COL4A3 splicing variant.
papers.summary: In a large Italian family with autosomal dominant Alport syndrome, the synonymous COL4A3 c.765G>A (p.(Thr255Thr)) variant segregated with disease and disrupted exon 13 splicing in patient-derived podocyte-lineage cells, producing an in-frame 28-amino-acid deletion. The study supports transcript analysis in disease-relevant cells and reports that ACE inhibitors may delay kidney failure, while CRISPR/Cas9 correction remains a proposed strategy rather than a tested therapy.
papers.why: The study demonstrates how deep genetic analysis and patient-derived podocytes identify and functionally validate a cryptic COL4A3 splicing variant causing autosomal dominant Alport syndrome.

papers.title: Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection: A Rare Manifestation of Alport Syndrome.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 36-year-old woman with X-linked Alport syndrome and a COL4A5 nonsense variant who developed spontaneous coronary artery dissection with an intimal flap in the mid left circumflex artery. Percutaneous balloon angioplasty and drug-eluting stent placement resolved her chest pain, but the proposed mechanism linking defective type IV collagen, uncontrolled hypertension, and coronary arterial wall vulnerability remains speculative.
papers.why: The report provides direct clinical evidence that percutaneous coronary angioplasty can relieve symptoms in the rare coronary manifestation of Alport syndrome.

papers.title: Angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitor therapy in children with Alport syndrome: effect on urinary albumin, TGF-beta, and nitrite excretion.
papers.summary: In 11 children with early Alport syndrome, 14 days of enalapril did not significantly reduce urinary albumin, TGF-β, or nitrite excretion, and GFR could not be assessed after treatment. The authors interpret the early disease as predominantly an intrinsic glomerular basement membrane barrier defect without evidence of increased TGF-β or nitric oxide production or an angiotensin II-sensitive hemodynamic protein leak, while acknowledging uncertainty about later-stage or long-term treatment.
papers.why: This study directly tested enalapril in children with early Alport syndrome and measured urinary albumin, TGF-beta, and nitrite as treatment-response and mechanistic outcomes.

papers.title: Treatment With Metformin in Chinese Children With Alport Syndrome
papers.summary: This single-center, prospective, double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trial will evaluate the efficacy and safety of metformin in Chinese children with Alport syndrome who have received (and continue to receive)) ACEi/ARB.

papers.title: A Study to Learn About How Well BAY 3401016 Works in Adults With Alport Syndrome
papers.summary: Alport syndrome (AS) is a rare genetic condition that causes kidney disease, hearing loss, and eye abnormalities that occur due to changes in specific genes (COL4A3, COL4A4, and COL4A5). These genes help in producing an important protein called collagen. People with AS have a high risk of developing chronic kidney disease (CKD), a condition in which there is progressive loss in kidney function over time. The kidneys soon lose their ability to remove waste products from the body properly, resulting in end-stage kidney disease. A common sign of decreasing kidney function is the presence of exces

papers.title: A Study of ELX-02 in Patients With Alport Syndrome
papers.summary:
This is a Phase 2 open label pilot study to evaluate the safety and efficacy of subcutaneously administered ELX-02 in patients with X-linked or autosomal recessive Alport Syndrome with Col4A5 and Col4A3/4 nonsense mutation.

In total, up to 8 participants, with a minimum of 3 adults, will be enrolled in the trial.

The study will be comprised of the following periods for each participant:

* a Screening period of up to 6 weeks (42 days)
* a total Treatment Period of 8 weeks (60 days)
* a safety/efficacy Follow-up Period of 12 weeks (90 days) after the last treatment The Treatment Period will b

papers.title: Study of Sparsentan Treatment in Pediatrics With Proteinuric Glomerular Diseases
papers.summary: To evaluate the safety, efficacy and tolerability of sparsentan oral suspension and tablets, and assess changes in proteinuria after once-daily dosing over 108 weeks.

papers.title: An Extended Access Program for Bardoxolone Methyl in Patients With CKD (EAGLE)
papers.summary: This extended access study will assess the long-term safety and tolerability of bardoxolone methyl in qualified patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) who previously participated in one of the qualifying clinical studies with bardoxolone methyl. Patients will remain in the study until bardoxolone methyl is available through commercial channels or until patient withdrawal, whichever is sooner.

papers.title: Effects of an Intensified Treatment With ACE-I,ATA II and Statins in Alport Syndrome
papers.summary: Alport syndrome (AS) represents a form of progressive hereditary nephritis in which the genetic defect resides in the synthesis of one of several subunits of type IV collagen, the predominant constituent of basement membranes in renal glomeruli. Renal impairment occurs with time and severe renal failure with hypertension and uremia represent the end stage of the disease, even if a high variability in the rate of progression is described.Males are usually affected by a progressive form of the disease. Affected females with X-linked syndrome usually have a good prognosis with a mild renal impair

papers.title: A Study to Evaluate Setanaxib in Patients With Alport Syndrome
papers.summary: The purpose of the study is to learn about the safety and tolerability of setanaxib in subjects with Alport syndrome, when added to their standard of care treatment. The study will assess how safe setanaxib is when compared to placebo. Study participants will be asked if they are experiencing any side effects at each study visit. In addition, tests in blood, urine and other examinations will be used to look at the safety of setanaxib. The study will also measure how well setanaxib works in comparison to a placebo, by measuring urine protein and certain markers in the blood and urine. The conce

papers.title: Study of Lademirsen (SAR339375) in Patients With Alport Syndrome
papers.summary:
Primary Objectives:

* To assess the efficacy of lademirsen (SAR339375) in reducing the decline in renal function.
* To assess the safety and tolerability of lademirsen (SAR339375) in participants with Alport syndrome.

Secondary Objectives:

* To assess plasma pharmacokinetic (PK) parameters of the parent compound and its active major metabolite.
* To assess the potential formation of anti-drug antibodies (ADAs) following administration of lademirsen (SAR339375).
* To assess the pharmacodynamic effect of lademirsen (SAR339375) on miR-21 and on changes in renal injury and function biomarkers.

papers.title: Study of Hydroxychloroquine in Patients With X-linked Alport Syndrome in China (CHXLAS)
papers.summary: This Phase 2 randomized controlled trial will study the safety, tolerability, and efficacy of Hydroxychloroquine in qualified patients with Alport syndrome. The trial will be open-label, randomized, controlled and will enroll up to 50 patients.

papers.title: Vonafexor ALPort Syndrome Efficacy & Safety TRIAl-1 (ALPESTRIA-1)
papers.summary: This study is a proof-of-concept trial of vonafexor safety, its effects on kidney function in subjects with at risk of progression Alport syndrome.

papers.title: Albuminuria Lowering Effect of Dapagliflozin, Spironolactone and Their Combination in Adult Patients With Alport Syndrome (COMBINE-ALPORT)
papers.summary: Alport syndrome (AS) is one of the most common monogenic kidney disorders, oftentimes leading to end-stage kidney disease (ESKD). As AS is caused by variants involving type IV collagen genes (COL4), there is no specific treatment aimed at stopping the disease progression. Large studies have validated the use of renin-angiotensin-system inhibitors (RASis) in AS, as these drugs can slow the progression to chronic kidney disease (CKD). These studies included mainly pediatric patients with X-linked AS (XLAS). There is a lack of data regarding the therapeutic approach in patients having autosomal d

papers.title: EXACT Study: A Blinded Study in Patients With Alport Syndrome to Evaluate Exaluren Efficacy and Safety
papers.summary:
This is a randomized, double-Blind, placebo-controlled study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of exaluren in Alport Syndrome patients with nonsense mutations in COL4A3/4/5 genes.

Targeted 24 patients aged 12 and older will be enrolled in the trial.

The study will be comprised of the following periods for each participant:

* a Screening period of up to 6 weeks (42 days)
* a total Treatment Period of exaluren 0.75 mg/kg or placebo administered daily subcutaneously for 32 weeks: Part 1: patients are randomized to either exaluren or placebo for 16 weeks. Part 2: all patients across both rand

papers.title: Human Umbilical Cord Mesenchymal Stem Cells for Alport Syndrome
papers.summary: The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the safety and efficacy of human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells (hUC-MSC) in the treatment of Alport syndrome (AS) in a randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled trial, to provide a clinical basis for the development of stem cell products for the treatment of AS, and to further clarify the therapeutic effect of hUC-MSC in the treatment of AS.

papers.title: A Study of RG-012 in Subjects With Alport Syndrome
papers.summary: This is a Phase 1, open-label, multi-center study of the safety, pharmacodynamics, and pharmacokinetics of RG-012 administered to subjects with Alport syndrome.

papers.title: Atrasentan in Patients With Proteinuric Glomerular Diseases
papers.summary: The AFFINITY Study is a phase 2, open-label, basket study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of atrasentan in patients with proteinuric glomerular disease who are at risk of progressive loss of renal function.

papers.title: Efficacy and Safety Study to Delay Renal Failure in Children With Alport Syndrome
papers.summary:
This is a phase III, multi-centre, randomised, placebo-controlled, patient and investigator-blind study in paediatric patients with early stages of Alport syndrome to assess the safety and efficacy of the ACEi ramipril in slowing disease progression.

Alport syndrome stages that describe the extent of renal damage and loss of function are defined as:

* 0 Microhaematuria without microalbuminuria (usually at birth)
* I Microalbuminuria (30-300 mg albumin/gCrea)
* II Proteinuria \>300 mg albumin/gCrea
* III \> 25% decline of normal renal function (creatinine clearance)
* IV End stage renal failu

papers.title: Study to Evaluate R3R01 in Patients With Alport Syndrome and Patients With Focal Segmental Glomerulosclerosis
papers.summary: This is a Phase 2, Multi-center, Open-Label Study to Assess Safety, Tolerability, Efficacy and Pharmacokinetics of R3R01 in Alport Syndrome Patients with Uncontrolled Proteinuria on ACE/ARB Inhibition and in Patients with Primary Steroid-Resistant Focal Segmental Glomerulosclerosis

papers.title: Safety and Efficacy of ACEI in Alport Syndrome Patients With COL4A3/COL4A4/COL4A5 Variants
papers.summary: Alport syndrome (AS) is the second most common monogenic cause of end-stage renal failure (ESRF). AS is caused by variants in the COL4A3, COL4A4, and COL4A5 genes, which encode for the a3, a4, and a5 chains of type IV collagen. This trial is a prospective, randomized, controlled and multicenter trial. Mainly to assess the safety and efficacy of ramipril in Alport syndrome patients with variants of COL4A3/COL4A4/COL4A5.

papers.title: A Phase 2/3 Trial of the Efficacy and Safety of Bardoxolone Methyl in Patients With Alport Syndrome - CARDINAL
papers.summary: This international, multi-center, Phase 2/3 trial will study the safety, tolerability, and efficacy of bardoxolone methyl in qualified patients with Alport syndrome. The Phase 2 portion of the trial will be open-label and enroll up to 30 patients. The Phase 3 portion of the trial will be double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled and will enroll up to 180 patients.

papers.title: Open Targets drug and clinical candidates for Alport syndrome
Open Targets drugs acting on COL4A3
The enhanced renin-angiotensin-aldosteron system pharmacological blockade--which is the best?.
papers.summary: In a randomized crossover trial of 18 patients with non-diabetic proteinuric chronic kidney disease, telmisartan plus aliskiren lowered albuminuria more than telmisartan plus eplerenone or telmisartan 160 mg monotherapy. The greater antiproteinuric effect of the angiotensin receptor blocker–renin inhibitor combination was independent of blood-pressure changes.

papers.title: Urinary Biomarkers and Kidney Injury in VA NEPHRON-D: Phenotyping Acute Kidney Injury in Clinical Trials.
papers.summary: In a VA NEPHRON-D substudy of diabetic chronic kidney disease, combination renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system blockade increased serum creatinine-defined acute kidney injury but left most urinary biomarkers unchanged or decreased them at 12 months. A pooled analysis found reduced albuminuria across three chronic kidney disease trials, suggesting that serum creatinine alone may incompletely characterize treatment-associated kidney injury.

papers.title: Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System Blockade in Diabetic Nephropathy. Present Evidences.
papers.summary: This review concludes that single renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system blockade with an ACE inhibitor or angiotensin receptor blocker reduces albuminuria and slows diabetic kidney disease progression, but does not reliably prevent progression to end-stage renal disease. Combination blockade improves short-term albuminuria yet increases acute kidney injury and hyperkalemia without improving hard renal outcomes, while mineralocorticoid receptor blockade and dietary sodium restriction may enhance antiproteinuric effects but lack definitive long-term evidence.

papers.title: Cardiovascular and Renal Outcomes with Finerenone, a Selective Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonist.
papers.summary: This review reports that overactivation of the renin–angiotensin–aldosterone system (RAAS) contributes to inflammation, fibrosis, proteinuria, and kidney-disease progression, providing a mechanistic rationale for mineralocorticoid receptor blockade. Finerenone reduced albuminuria and kidney progression in clinical trials involving diabetic CKD, generally with less hyperkalemia and less blood-pressure reduction than steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, but its effects in HFpEF and non-diabetic CKD remain limited or unestablished.

papers.title: Real-Life Experience on the Effect of SGLT2 Inhibitors vs. Finerenone vs. Combination on Albuminuria in Chronic Kidney Disease.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 98 adults with chronic kidney disease and albuminuria, sequential SGLT2 inhibitor–finerenone combination therapy produced a greater reduction in urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio than either monotherapy. Combination therapy was not associated with greater hyperkalemia than SGLT2 inhibitor monotherapy or a statistically significant between-group difference in estimated glomerular filtration rate decline, although the retrospective, small, single-center design limits causal and long-term conclusions.

papers.title: AMPK mediates regulation of glomerular volume and podocyte survival.
papers.summary: The study shows that AMPK activation limits glomerular enlargement and protects podocytes from podocyte loss in Shroom3-knockdown and nephrectomy models. Metformin and PF0640957 reduced podocyte loss and glomerular injury in mice, whereas AMPK inhibition with Compound C promoted podocyte loss; human MCD glomerular transcriptomes showed enrichment of AMPK-related signaling compared with FSGS.

papers.title: Adriamycin-induced podocyte injury via the Sema3A/TRPC5/Rac1 pathway.
papers.summary: In Adriamycin-induced podocyte injury, the paper identifies a Sema3A–TRPC5–Rac1 cytoskeletal pathway, while urinary Sema3A correlates with the podocyte marker podocalyxin in patients with podocytopathies. TRPC5 inhibition with AC1903 reduces podocyte apoptosis and foot-process effacement and lowers proteinuria in cultured podocytes and Adriamycin-treated BALB/c mice, but the study did not directly demonstrate rescue of podocyte loss or efficacy in Alport syndrome.

papers.title: Elevated Prorenin Induces Podocyte Injury and Glomerular Fibrosis in cyp1a1-Prorenin Transgenic Rats.
papers.summary: In an inducible liver-specific prorenin rat model, elevated circulating prorenin caused podocyte loss, albuminuria, hypertension, and glomerular fibrosis independently of hyperglycemia. Amlodipine and enalapril partially rescued podocyte loss and reduced fibrosis by suppressing NF-κB- and Nox2-associated inflammatory and oxidative signaling, but did not normalize circulating prorenin or fully reverse injury.

papers.title: <i>LAMA5</i> pathogenic variant uncovers a novel autoantigen in membranous nephropathy.
