papers.summary: A pediatric membranous nephropathy case and a Lama5N457I knock-in mouse model show that the LAMA5 p.N452I variant increases Laminin α5 binding to Collagen IV, causes glomerular basement membrane thickening, and induces conformation-specific anti-Laminin α5 IgG1/IgG3 autoantibodies that activate classical complement and promote podocyte injury. Rituximab eliminated circulating anti-Laminin α5 autoantibodies and accompanied sustained clinical remission, while COL4A3/4/5-related Alport syndrome showed basement membrane abnormalities without detectable glomerular IgG deposition.

papers.title: Acarbose ameliorates podocyte injury and glomerular lesions in diabetic nephropathy through USP46 activation.
papers.summary: The paper identifies reduced podocyte USP46 expression in diabetic nephropathy and shows that podocyte-specific Usp46 deletion worsens diabetic podocyte injury, albuminuria, and glomerular lesions. Acarbose activates USP46, reduces TDP-43 aggregation, prevents podocyte loss, and mitigates albuminuria in diabetic mice, with efficacy abolished in Usp46 PKO mice.

papers.title: Evaluation of Puromycin-Induced Podocyte Injury and Protective Effects of Voclosporin Using Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells from a Patient with Nephrotic Syndrome Harboring an <i>INF2</i> Variant.
papers.summary: Patient-derived kidney organoids carrying an INF2 variant modeled puromycin aminonucleoside-induced podocyte injury and enabled assessment of podocyte-protective therapies. Cyclosporine A and voclosporin reduced injury and preserved podocalyxin expression to similar extents, demonstrating direct protection in this in-vitro genetic FSGS platform.

papers.title: Dual deficiency of angiotensin-converting enzyme-2 and Mas receptor enhances angiotensin II-induced hypertension and hypertensive nephropathy.
papers.summary: In an Ang II-infused mouse model, deletion of ACE2, Mas, or both enhanced hypertension, renal dysfunction, fibrosis, and inflammation; dual deletion produced the most severe disease through AT1–ERK1/2–Smad3 and Smurf2–Smad7–NF-κB signaling. The findings identify the angiotensin-converting enzyme 2/angiotensin-[1–7]/Mas receptor axis as a protective mechanistic target, while cited evidence supports human recombinant ACE2, angiotensin-[1–7], losartan, and PD98059 as potentially transferable interventions.

papers.title: Combined sodium glucose co-transporter-2 inhibitor and angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibition upregulates the renin-angiotensin system in chronic kidney disease with type 2 diabetes: Results of a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled exploratory trial.
papers.summary: In a 12-week randomized trial, empagliflozin added to enalapril or ramipril increased plasma renin activity, angiotensin I, and angiotensin-(1–7) in patients with diabetic CKD, consistent with modulation toward the alternative renin–angiotensin system. The molecular response was weaker or absent in non-diabetic CKD, and ACE2 levels remained suppressed, so the trial did not directly establish a durable clinical benefit or the enzyme responsible for angiotensin-(1–7) generation.

papers.title: Add-On Cyclic Angiotensin-(1-7) with Cyclophosphamide Arrests Progressive Kidney Disease in Rats with ANCA Associated Glomerulonephritis.
papers.summary: The study shows that adding lanthionine-stabilized cyclic angiotensin-(1-7), or cAng-(1-7), to cyclophosphamide in MPO-ANCA-associated crescentic glomerulonephritis rats markedly improved proteinuria, renal histology, inflammation, endothelial injury, and glomerular structural preservation compared with vehicle or cyclophosphamide alone. The paper identifies the ACE2/Ang-(1-7)/Mas receptor axis as the renoprotective mechanism and cites prior experimental renoprotection of Ang-(1-7) in Alport syndrome, but does not test treatment in Alport syndrome itself.

papers.title: Angiotensin-(1-7) Mitigates Progression from Acute Kidney Injury to Chronic Kidney Disease Via Renin-Angiotensin System Modulation in a Murine Model.
papers.summary: In a murine bilateral renal ischemia-reperfusion model, Ang-(1–7) shifted the renin-angiotensin system toward its protective arm, reduced inflammatory and fibrotic signaling, restored antioxidant activity, and mitigated acute kidney injury progression toward chronic kidney disease. This provides experimental support for targeting the angiotensin-converting enzyme 2/angiotensin-[1–7]/Mas receptor axis as a transferable renal strategy, but efficacy in Alport syndrome or humans was not tested.

papers.title: Addition of cyclic angiotensin-(1-7) to angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor therapy has a positive add-on effect in experimental diabetic nephropathy.
papers.summary: In BTBR ob/ob mice with type 2 diabetic nephropathy, the peptidase-resistant lanthipeptide cyclic angiotensin-(1-7) limited albuminuria and podocyte dysfunction, reduced glomerular fibrosis and inflammation, and counteracted glomerular capillary rarefaction. Adding cyclic angiotensin-(1-7) to lisinopril produced a superior antiproteinuric effect than lisinopril alone, with improved preservation of podocyte proteins and capillary density.

papers.title: The antihypertensive action of C-phycocyanin is related to the prevention of angiotensin II-caused vascular dysfunction in chronic kidney disease.
papers.summary: In 5/6-nephrectomized rats, chronic kidney disease increased angiotensin II-mediated vasoconstriction, reduced angiotensin 1-7-mediated vasorelaxation, and increased AT1/AT2 while reducing Mas receptor expression. Oral C-phycocyanin prevented systemic arterial hypertension, renal function impairment, and these angiotensin-system vascular changes.

papers.title: Both ERK/MAPK and TGF-Beta/Smad signaling pathways play a role in the kidney fibrosis of diabetic mice accelerated by blood glucose fluctuation.
papers.summary: In an alloxan-induced mouse model, repetitive blood glucose fluctuation accelerated diabetic renal fibrosis by increasing type I collagen and TGF-β1, reducing MMP1, increasing TIMP1, and activating transforming growth factor-beta/Smad signaling, particularly through increased Smad2 phosphorylation. The study also found increased ERK/MAPK signaling but unchanged p38 and AKT signaling, and cited kidney-targeted Smad7 gene transfer as a transferable approach for suppressing TGF-beta/Smad signaling in diabetic nephropathy.

papers.title: Rhubarb Protect Against Tubulointerstitial Fibrosis by Inhibiting TGF-β/Smad Pathway and Improving Abnormal Metabolome in Chronic Kidney Disease.
papers.summary: In male Sprague-Dawley rats with adenine-induced chronic kidney disease, rhubarb extracts reduced tubulointerstitial fibrosis and renal injury by rebalancing transforming growth factor-beta/Smad signaling, lowering multiple profibrotic pathway proteins while increasing Smad7. The extracts also improved renal biochemical abnormalities and partially normalized a validated panel of altered tissue metabolites, providing an experimental anti-fibrotic intervention potentially transferable to Alport syndrome.

papers.title: Deubiquitinase inhibitor PR-619 reduces Smad4 expression and suppresses renal fibrosis in mice with unilateral ureteral obstruction.
papers.summary: In a mouse unilateral ureteral obstruction model and TGF-β1-stimulated NRK-49F rat renal fibroblasts, the pan-deubiquitinase inhibitor PR-619 reduced renal fibrosis and selectively reduced Smad4 expression without reducing TGF-β receptors, Smad2, or Smad3. These findings support modulation of transforming growth factor-beta/Smad signaling as a transferable anti-fibrotic strategy, although the responsible deubiquitinase remains unidentified.

papers.title: Cathepsin S regulates renal fibrosis in mouse models of mild and severe hydronephrosis.
papers.summary: In mouse models of mild and severe hydronephrosis and in TGF-β1-stimulated TCMK-1 tubular epithelial cells, CTSS expression was associated with renal fibrosis, extracellular matrix deposition, epithelial-mesenchymal transition, and transforming growth factor-beta/Smad signaling. Importantly, both pharmacological inhibition with LY3000328 and CTSS-targeting siRNA increased fibrotic and signaling markers under the tested conditions, worsening rather than rescuing fibrosis.

papers.title: Microparticles derived from human erythropoietin mRNA-transfected mesenchymal stem cells inhibit epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and ameliorate renal interstitial fibrosis.
papers.summary: In TGF-β1-treated MDCK cells, hEPO-MPs delivered EPO mRNA and attenuated epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition by reducing Smad2, Smad3, and p38 MAPK signaling. In the unilateral ureteral obstruction mouse model, a single intravenous hEPO-MP treatment reduced renal tubulointerstitial fibrosis, myofibroblast accumulation, EMT markers, and macrophage infiltration comparably to repeated high-dose rhEPO.

papers.title: Protective effect of yacon leaves extract (Smallanthus sonchifolius (Poepp.) H. Rob) through antifibrosis, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant mechanisms toward diabetic nephropathy.
papers.summary: In glucose-induced mouse mesangial cells modeling diabetic nephropathy, ethanolic yacon leaves extract reduced TGF-β1 and the expression of SMAD2, SMAD3, and SMAD4 while increasing SMAD7, indicating modulation of transforming growth factor-beta/Smad signaling. The extract also reduced mesangial-cell proliferation, TNF-α, and malondialdehyde, supporting antifibrotic, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant effects in this in vitro model.

papers.title: Combined paracrine and endocrine AAV9 mediated expression of hepatocyte growth factor for the treatment of renal fibrosis.
papers.summary: In COL4A3-deficient mice, intravenous rAAV9-CMV-Ksp-hHGF enabled combined endocrine expression in liver and paracrine expression in renal tubular epithelium. The treatment attenuated tubulointerstitial fibrosis and reduced the fibrotic markers Col1A1, PDGFR-beta, and alpha-smooth muscle actin.

papers.title: Atypical anti-glomerular basement membrane disease.
papers.summary: This five-patient series documents atypical anti-glomerular basement membrane disease ranging from indolent renal abnormalities to abrupt necrotizing and crescentic glomerulonephritis. The disease directly involves the collagen α3α4α5(IV) network through autoantibodies, but no intervention tested here corrects or stabilizes that network; clinical improvement was observed with immunosuppressive treatment in individual patients.

papers.title: <i>Drosophila</i> SPARC collagen IV chaperone-like activity essential for development is unique to the fat body.
papers.summary: In Drosophila, fat body-derived SPARC acts as a collagen IV chaperone that enables collagen IV diffusion and incorporation into basement membranes, and loss of this activity is lethal. The SPARC domain II/III fragment retains sufficient collagen IV chaperone-like activity to restore collagen IV delivery and rescue SPARC-null larvae to adulthood, even though the fragment cannot diffuse beyond the hemolymph.

papers.title: T cell, M2 macrophage infiltration and collagen, fibronectin, VCAM-1 expression portend poor outcome in lupus nephritis.
papers.summary: The study shows that pretreatment spatial proteomic profiles in kidney biopsies distinguish immunosuppressive-treatment nonresponders among patients with class IV or class V lupus nephritis. It identifies immune infiltration, collagen I/IV and fibronectin deposition, and VCAM-1 expression as outcome-associated markers, but it does not study or act on the collagen α3α4α5(IV) network and therefore provides no direct intervention evidence for transfer to Alport syndrome.

papers.title: High affinity binding of latent matrix metalloproteinase-9 to the alpha2(IV) chain of collagen IV.
papers.summary: The paper shows that pro-matrix metalloproteinase-9 binds with high affinity to the alpha2(IV) chain of collagen IV on MCF10A cells and other cell lines, while the closely related pro-matrix metalloproteinase-2 binds less strongly. Cell-surface binding does not activate or internalize pro-matrix metalloproteinase-9, including when complexed with tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinase-1, and pro-matrix metalloproteinase-9 does not bind triple-helical collagen IV.

papers.title: Development and characterization of a recombinant truncated type VII collagen "minigene". Implication for gene therapy of dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa.
papers.summary: A truncated recombinant type VII collagen minigene was produced and introduced into type VII collagen-deficient keratinocytes from dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa. The gene-corrected cells secreted correctly folded minicollagen VII and showed adhesion, proliferation, and motility changes that shifted the disease phenotype toward normal, but functional skin rescue was not demonstrated.

unread.title: DNA variant databases improve test accuracy and phenotype prediction in Alport syndrome.
unread.why: The paper describes a free, shared COL4A5 variant database that improves variant interpretation, diagnostic accuracy, and phenotype prediction for X-linked Alport syndrome.

unread.title: Identification of a Novel COL4A4 Variant in Compound-Heterozygous State in a Patient With Alport Syndrome and Histological Findings Similar to Focal Segmental Glomerulosclerosis (FSGS).
unread.why: The study demonstrates targeted NGS and Sanger sequencing as rapid, accurate approaches for identifying compound-heterozygous COL4A4 variants in a patient with Alport syndrome.

unread.title: The heterozygous mutation <i>COL4A4</i> c.817-1G>A causes Alport syndrome in a Chinese family: a case report.
unread.why: The report provides molecular diagnostic and functional RNA-splicing evidence for a COL4A4 variant causing autosomal dominant Alport syndrome.

unread.title: Clinical practice recommendations for the diagnosis and management of Alport syndrome in children, adolescents, and young adults-an update for 2020.
unread.why: This clinical-practice update provides actionable treatment timing, monitoring, and diagnostic recommendations for Alport syndrome in children and young adults.

unread.title: Autosomal dominant Alport syndrome linked to the type IV collage alpha 3 and alpha 4 genes (COL4A3 and COL4A4).
unread.why: The study links autosomal dominant Alport syndrome to COL4A3/COL4A4 variation using genetic linkage and mutation analysis and documents characteristic renal ultrastructure.

unread.title: Alport syndrome and thin glomerular basement membrane nephropathy: a practical approach to diagnosis.
unread.why: The review establishes a combined electron-microscopy and collagen-chain immunohistology workflow for distinguishing Alport syndrome from related thin-basement-membrane disorders.

unread.title: Novel COL4A5, COL4A4, and COL4A3 mutations in Alport syndrome.
unread.why: The study reports a large series of clinically useful COL4A3/4/5 mutation detections, achieving a 90% detection rate in patients with typical Alport phenotypes.

unread.title: Mild X-linked Alport syndrome due to the COL4A5 G624D variant originating in the Middle Ages is predominant in Central/East Europe and causes kidney failure in midlife.
unread.why: The national registry identifies and characterizes a predominant COL4A5 founder variant while providing clinically useful genotype-specific prognosis and natural-history outcomes.

unread.title: Skin biopsy is a practical approach for the clinical diagnosis and molecular genetic analysis of X-linked Alport's syndrome.
unread.why: This study validates skin biopsy with α5(IV) immunostaining and fibroblast cDNA analysis for early clinical diagnosis and mutation detection in X-linked Alport syndrome.

unread.title: Lifelong effect of therapy in young patients with the COL4A5 Alport missense variant p.(Gly624Asp): a prospective cohort study.
unread.why: A prospective cohort provides direct evidence that early ACE-inhibitor treatment can delay ESRF in patients with the COL4A5 p.(Gly624Asp) variant.

unread.title: A founder COL4A4 pathogenic variant resulting in autosomal recessive Alport syndrome accounts for most genetic kidney failure in Romani people.
unread.why: NGS testing in a defined cohort identifies recurrent COL4A3 and COL4A4 founder variants and provides clinically actionable genotype-phenotype data in Alport syndrome.

unread.title: A novel mouse model for X-linked Alport syndrome induced by splicing mutation in the Col4a5 gene.
unread.why: The paper develops and characterizes a new X-linked Alport mouse model for studying disease mechanisms and treatment responses.

unread.title: Clinical utility of genetic testing in early-onset kidney disease: seven genes are the main players.
unread.why: The kidney gene panel produced a 65% diagnostic yield in early-onset CKD and was among the leading tests for COL4A3, COL4A4, and COL4A5-related disease.

unread.title: Identification of 47 novel mutations in patients with Alport syndrome and thin basement membrane nephropathy.
unread.why: Testing 216 individuals identified 47 novel Alport or thin-basement-membrane variants and expanded the diagnostic variant spectrum for COL4A3, COL4A4, and COL4A5.

unread.title: Nine novel COL4A3 and COL4A4 mutations and polymorphisms identified in inherited membrane diseases.
unread.why: The study identifies three pathogenic variants and six polymorphisms, providing diagnostic reference sequences for distinguishing Alport and thin-basement-membrane variants from uncommon benign alleles.

unread.title: Collagen type IV-related nephropathies in Portugal: pathogenic COL4A3 and COL4A4 mutations and clinical characterization of 25 families.
unread.why: The study validates a three-gene sequencing approach for suspected collagen IV-related nephropathy and reports diagnostic yield and phenotype correlations in 40 probands.

unread.title: Glomerular Basement Membrane Protein Expression and the Diagnosis and Prognosis of Autosomal Dominant Alport Syndrome.
unread.why: The case provides measured glomerular protein-staining patterns proposed to distinguish autosomal dominant Alport syndrome from thin basement membrane nephropathy and inform prognosis.

unread.title: Kidney Disease Associated With Mono-allelic COL4A3 and COL4A4 Variants: A Case Series of 17 Families.
unread.why: This 42-person study demonstrates sequencing, segregation, biopsy, and longitudinal clinical methods for characterizing mono-allelic COL4A3/COL4A4 kidney disease.

unread.title: Mutation analysis of COL4A3 and COL4A4 genes in a Chinese autosomal-dominant Alport syndrome family.
unread.why: The study reports direct sequencing-based identification and segregation analysis of two potentially causal COL4A4 variants in a large autosomal dominant Alport syndrome family.

unread.title: Phenotype-genotype correlations in patients with Alport syndrome from the Polish population.
unread.why: The 77-patient study provides direct data on NGS and Sanger confirmation, phenotype-genotype associations, and early renal, hearing, and ocular findings in suspected Alport syndrome.

unread.title: Case Report: Whole genome sequencing identifies a novel deep intronic <i>COL4A5</i> variant of uncertain significance in X-linked Alport syndrome.
unread.why: The case demonstrates that whole-genome sequencing can identify an elusive deep intronic COL4A5 variant when targeted testing and biopsy-based diagnosis are inconclusive.

unread.title: [Diffuse esophageal leiomyomatosis and Alport's syndrome: A case report and review of the literature].
unread.why: The report provides a diagnostic skin-biopsy clue and a surgical management approach for the diffuse leiomyomatosis phenotype associated with Alport syndrome.

unread.title: Lithuanian Study on <i>COL4A3</i> and <i>COL4A4</i> Genetic Variants in Alport Syndrome: Clinical Characterization of 52 Individuals from 38 Families.
unread.why: The 221-person screening study provides diagnostic and clinical outcome data for Alport syndrome and adds 18 variants to global genetic databases.

unread.title: Bull terrier hereditary nephritis: a model for autosomal dominant Alport syndrome.
unread.why: The study establishes a dog model with renal failure, hematuria, anterior lenticonus, and characteristic glomerular basement membrane lesions relevant to Alport syndrome.

unread.title: Searching for a treatment for Alport syndrome using mouse models.
unread.why: This review summarizes tested Alport mouse models and interventions, including effective ACE inhibition and experimental stem-cell and genetic approaches.

unread.title: A novel model of autosomal dominant Alport syndrome in Dalmatian dogs.
unread.why: The study characterizes a spontaneous canine model with dominant inheritance, renal failure, glomerular sclerosis, fibrosis, and lamellated glomerular basement membranes.

unread.title: Early angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibition in Alport syndrome delays renal failure and improves life expectancy.
unread.why: Long-term clinical data show that early ACE inhibition delays renal failure and improves life expectancy in Alport syndrome.

unread.title: Collagen COL4A3 knockout: a mouse model for autosomal Alport syndrome.
unread.why: The COL4A3 knockout mouse reproduces progressive glomerulonephritis, basement-membrane abnormalities, proteinuria, and renal failure relevant to Alport syndrome.

unread.title: Improving mutation screening in familial hematuric nephropathies through next generation sequencing.
unread.why: This study demonstrates an efficient NGS workflow that identifies mutations, indels, and large rearrangements in all major Alport syndrome genes.

unread.title: Natural history of genetically proven autosomal recessive Alport syndrome.
unread.why: The study validated a three-step genetic diagnostic strategy in genetically proven autosomal recessive Alport syndrome and also provides a median ESRD onset estimate.

unread.title: X-linked Alport syndrome: an SSCP-based mutation survey over all 51 exons of the COL4A5 gene.
unread.why: This large X-linked Alport cohort tested an exon-wide SSCP mutation screen, although its 45% detection rate reveals important limitations.

unread.title: Rapid identification of a disease allele in mouse through whole genome sequencing and bulk segregation analysis.
unread.why: The paper created a Col4a4-null nephritis model and demonstrated an efficient whole-genome sequencing plus segregation workflow for identifying causal renal-disease alleles.

unread.title: Detection of mutations in COL4A5 in patients with Alport syndrome.
unread.why: The assay detected COL4A5 mutations in 77 of 153 suspected Alport families and was explicitly used for diagnostic confirmation, carrier screening, and phenotype correlation.

unread.title: Outcomes of male patients with Alport syndrome undergoing renal replacement therapy.
unread.why: This multicenter registry study provides real-world comparative outcome data for dialysis and kidney transplantation in men with Alport syndrome.

unread.title: Alport retinopathy results from "severe" COL4A5 mutations and predicts early renal failure.
unread.why: The study identifies severe COL4A5-associated retinopathy as a clinically measurable marker predicting early renal failure in X-linked Alport syndrome.

unread.title: Detection of mutations in the COL4A5 gene by analyzing cDNA of skin fibroblasts.
unread.why: This study validates a high-sensitivity COL4A5 mutation-detection method in cultured skin fibroblasts for X-linked Alport syndrome, including cryptic splice variants.

unread.title: A Split-Luciferase-Based Trimer Formation Assay as a High-throughput Screening Platform for Therapeutics in Alport Syndrome.
unread.why: The paper develops an Alport-specific high-throughput assay and identifies chemical chaperones and RNA strategies that restore mutant type IV collagen trimerization.

unread.title: Detection of mutations in the COL4A5 gene by SSCP in X-linked Alport syndrome.
unread.why: The study reports a PCR-SSCP mutation-screening assay with clinical validation in suspected X-linked Alport syndrome.

unread.title: Mutations in the codon for a conserved arginine-1563 in the COL4A5 collagen gene in Alport syndrome.
unread.why: The study uses validated molecular screening methods to identify disease-causing COL4A5 mutations in Alport syndrome kindreds.

unread.title: Novel Keap1-Nrf2 Protein-Protein Interaction Inhibitor UBE-1099 Ameliorates Progressive Phenotype in Alport Syndrome Mouse Model.
unread.why: The study directly tests the therapeutic drug UBE-1099 in an Alport mouse model and reports reduced proteinuria, improved glomerulosclerosis and fibrosis, and prolonged lifespan.

unread.title: Detection of 12 novel mutations in the collagenous domain of the COL4A5 gene in Alport syndrome patients.
unread.why: SSCP screening detected 12 genuine COL4A5 mutations in a cohort diagnosed with Alport syndrome, providing a concrete mutation-screening method.

unread.title: Long-term ACE inhibition in Alport syndrome: are the benefits worth the risks?
unread.why: The randomized EARLY PRO-TECT evidence supports ramipril as an early renoprotective intervention that slows albuminuria and eGFR decline in children with Alport syndrome.

unread.title: Mutant-type alpha5(IV) collagen in a mild form of Alport syndrome has residual ability to form a heterotrimer.
unread.why: Engineered mutant alpha5(IV) collagen and functional secretion assays explain how residual heterotrimer formation produces a mild Alport phenotype.

unread.title: Twenty-one novel mutations identified in the COL4A5 gene in Chinese patients with X-linked Alport's syndrome confirmed by skin biopsy.
unread.why: Direct COL4A5 sequencing identified 25 pathogenic variants in Chinese families, while skin biopsy provided an effective diagnostic confirmation.

unread.title: De novo mutations in COL4A5 identified by whole exome sequencing in 2 girls with Alport syndrome in Korea.
unread.why: Whole-exome sequencing detected de novo COL4A5 variants in two girls with Alport syndrome and was proposed as an effective diagnostic approach when family history is absent.

unread.title: Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress Activation in Alport Syndrome Varies Between Genotype and Cell Type.
unread.why: The study supplies Alport-specific cellular models and shows that genotype- and cell-dependent ER-stress markers can model mutant collagen effects.

unread.title: Molecular Review of Suspected Alport Syndrome Patients-A Single-Centre Experience.
unread.why: A targeted NGS panel established a molecular diagnosis in 79% of probands and supported carrier testing, inheritance determination, prognosis, and selection of renoprotective care.

unread.title: Clinical trial recommendations for potential Alport syndrome therapies.
unread.why: This consensus resource provides concrete standards for preclinical translation, biomarkers, trial design, pediatric recruitment, and outcome selection in Alport syndrome trials.

unread.title: The multifaceted phenotypic and genotypic spectrum of type-IV-collagen-related nephropathy-A human genetics department experience.
unread.why: Exome sequencing and interdisciplinary genotype-phenotype review diagnosed and reclassified type-IV-collagen nephropathy cases with heterogeneous presentations.

unread.title: Four novel mutations identified in the COL4A3, COL4A4 and COL4A5 genes in 10 families with Alport syndrome.
unread.why: Whole-exome sequencing plus cellular functional testing identified and characterized pathogenic COL4A3, COL4A4, and COL4A5 variants in Alport families.

unread.title: Reassessing the pathogenicity of c.2858G>T(p.(G953V)) in COL4A5 Gene: report of 19 Chinese families.
unread.why: Analysis of 19 families reclassified COL4A5 c.2858G>T as benign and provided a concrete diagnostic rule to prevent Alport syndrome misdiagnosis based on this variant alone.

unread.title: Anticodon-edited tRNA enables translational readthrough of COL4A5 premature termination codons.
unread.why: Anticodon-edited tRNAs restored full-length COL4A5 translation and α3α4α5 heterotrimer formation for four patient-derived nonsense variants in cell-based assays.

unread.title: Genetic, Clinical, and Pathologic Backgrounds of Children With X-Linked Alport Syndrome in China: A Monocenter Study.
unread.why: The pediatric cohort provides direct evidence for combining renal histology, COL4A5 staining, and NGS to diagnose and characterize X-linked Alport syndrome.

unread.title: Ocular Coherence Tomography Unveils Alport Syndrome: A Critical Tool in Detecting Collagen IV Nephropathies.
unread.why: OCT detected severe temporal macular thinning in genetically confirmed Alport cases and was proposed as an adjunct for differentiating Alport syndrome from primary FSGS.

unread.title: Effects of a Novel COL4A3 Homozygous/Heterozygous Splicing Mutation on the Mild Phenotype in a Family With Autosomal Recessive Alport Syndrome and a Literature Review.
unread.why: The combination of an in vitro minigene assay, bioinformatics, and biopsy staining experimentally confirms the pathogenic splicing effect of the COL4A3 variant.

unread.title: High adherence to angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor in children and adolescents with Alport syndrome: objective verification using liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry.
unread.why: The validated urine LC-MS assay accurately quantified recent ramipril intake and enabled objective measurement of ACE-inhibitor adherence in the Alport trial cohort.

unread.title: Pregnancy in women with autosomal recessive Alport syndrome caused by novel compound heterozygous mutations of COL4A3 gene: Two cases reports.
unread.why: Two pregnancies in autosomal recessive Alport syndrome were managed with supportive and antiproteinuric treatments, while genetic testing and renal pathology established the diagnosis.

unread.title: Case of maternal uniparental isodisomy with autosomal recessive Alport syndrome combined with congenital myasthenia and Oguchi disease.
unread.why: The case provides treatment-response and diagnostic data in COL4A4-associated Alport syndrome, including ARB therapy, exome analysis, and characteristic basement-membrane and collagen staining.

unread.title: Identification of mutations in the COL4A5 collagen gene in Alport syndrome.
unread.why: Direct identification of causal COL4A5 structural variants in Alport kindreds established a gene-based diagnostic approach.

unread.title: Unbiased next generation sequencing analysis confirms the existence of autosomal dominant Alport syndrome in a relevant fraction of cases.
unread.why: Targeted NGS in 87 families identified pathogenic variants across major Alport genes and was proposed as a first-level diagnostic analysis.

unread.title: Autosomal dominant Alport syndrome: molecular analysis of the COL4A4 gene and clinical outcome.
unread.why: The study provides a molecular testing strategy and clinical follow-up framework for differentiating autosomal dominant Alport syndrome from benign familial hematuria.

unread.title: Renal transplantation in patients with Alport syndrome.
unread.why: The review presents kidney transplantation and its genotype-guided donor and post-transplant monitoring requirements as established management solutions in Alport syndrome.

unread.title: Cyclosporine a slows the progressive renal disease of alport syndrome (X-linked hereditary nephritis): results from a canine model.
unread.why: In a canine model of X-linked Alport syndrome, cyclosporine A delayed GBM deterioration, reduced sclerosis, and slowed renal functional decline.

unread.title: A Neutralizing IL-11 Antibody Improves Renal Function and Increases Lifespan in a Mouse Model of Alport Syndrome.
unread.why: IL-11 neutralization improved renal function, reduced fibrosis and inflammation, and synergized with ramipril to extend lifespan in an Alport syndrome mouse model.

unread.title: The value of clinical criteria in identifying patients with X-linked Alport syndrome.
unread.why: In 206 patients, the study quantifies how clinical criteria and molecular testing identify COL4A5-related Alport syndrome and provides a practical diagnostic strategy.

unread.title: Hereditary nephritis (Alport's syndrome)--clinical profile and inheritance in 28 kindreds.
unread.why: This 28-kindred cohort provides longitudinal-style clinical, renal, auditory, ocular, and biopsy data useful for natural-history studies and outcome selection in Alport syndrome.

unread.title: Somatic mosaicism for a mutation of the COL4A5 gene is a cause of mild phenotype male Alport syndrome.
unread.why: This case demonstrates a multimodal molecular workflow detecting a pathogenic COL4A5 somatic mosaic variant in urine-derived RNA and renal tissue.

unread.title: Contemporary diagnostic approach in Alport's syndrome.
unread.why: It outlines an integrated diagnostic approach, including the clinically useful skin-biopsy assay with approximately 75% sensitivity for X-linked Alport syndrome.

unread.title: Urine-derived podocytes-lineage cells: A promising tool for precision medicine in Alport Syndrome.
unread.why: The study establishes urine-derived podocyte-lineage cells as a disease-relevant cellular model and molecular diagnostic platform for Alport spliceogenic variants.

unread.title: How benign is hematuria? Using genetics to predict prognosis.
unread.why: The review supports clinical genetic testing as a diagnostic and prognostic tool for children and young adults with persistent hematuria, including Alport syndrome.

unread.title: Alport syndrome: deducing the mode of inheritance from the presence of haematuria in family members.
unread.why: The paper provides practical pedigree and genetic-testing methods to distinguish X-linked and autosomal Alport syndrome and estimate risk in relatives.

unread.title: Structure of the human type IV collagen COL4A6 gene, which is mutated in Alport syndrome-associated leiomyomatosis.
unread.why: The study provides the complete COL4A6 exon-intron map and experimentally assigned restriction fragments that can support mutation and contiguous-deletion analysis in Alport syndrome-associated leiomyomatosis.

unread.title: Absence of the alpha6(IV) chain of collagen type IV in Alport syndrome is related to a failure at the protein assembly level and does not result in diffuse leiomyomatosis.
unread.why: The canine hereditary nephritis model and cell-based collagen-chain measurements directly investigate a mechanistic feature of X-linked Alport syndrome.

unread.title: Novel COL4A3 mutations in African American siblings with autosomal recessive Alport syndrome.
unread.why: The report identifies causal compound-heterozygous COL4A3 variants and supports complete sequencing as a diagnostic method in autosomal recessive Alport syndrome.

unread.title: Clear lens phacoemulsification in Alport syndrome: refractive results and electron microscopic analysis of the anterior lens capsule.
unread.why: Across 23 eyes, the study demonstrates clear lens phacoemulsification with lens implantation as an effective treatment of Alport anterior lenticonus and supports capsule ultrastructural diagnosis.

unread.title: Case Report: Preimplantation Genetic Testing and Pregnancy Outcomes in Women With Alport Syndrome.
unread.why: The study demonstrates feasible reproductive genetic testing in Alport syndrome and provides outcome data suggesting baseline proteinuria can inform counseling for pregnancy risk.

unread.title: COL4A4 gene study of a European population: description of new mutations causing autosomal dominant Alport syndrome.
unread.why: The clinical genetic study validates a concrete screening and sequencing workflow that identified two pathogenic COL4A4 variants in autosomal dominant Alport syndrome.

unread.title: A Novel COL4A4 Mutation Identified in a Chinese Family with Thin Basement Membrane Nephropathy.
unread.why: The study provides genetic and transcript-based testing for a COL4A4-related thin-basement-membrane nephropathy closely overlapping with autosomal Alport syndrome.

unread.title: Variants of Alport's syndrome.
unread.why: Indirect immunofluorescence with the GBM-reactive monoclonal antibody MCA-P1 identified an abnormal or inaccessible GBM antigen in a subset of patients with hereditary nephritis/Alport phenotypes.

unread.title: Bilateral serous retinal detachment associated with Alport's syndrome.
unread.why: Intensive hemodialysis resolved bilateral exudative retinal detachment and restored vision in a reported patient with Alport syndrome.
